claims.statement: A ghostly spirit of Welsh mythology (Wales), a moaning voice before death; linked to the River Tywi, eastern Dyfed and the Glamorganshire coast.
claims.statement_id: Roh hantu mitologi Welsh (Wales), suara rintihan sebelum kematian; dikaitkan dengan Sungai Tywi (River Tywi), Dyfed timur, dan pesisir Glamorganshire.
claims.quote: is a ghostly spirit in Welsh mythology, a disembodied moaning voice that sounds before a person's death. Legends associate the cyhyraeth with the area around the River Tywi in eastern Dyfed, as well as the coast of Glamorganshire.

claims.statement: Sounds three times as a warning; on the Glamorganshire coast before a shipwreck, with a corpse-light.
claims.statement_id: Terdengar tiga kali sebagai peringatan; di pesisir Glamorganshire sebelum kapal karam, dengan cahaya mayat (corpse-light).
claims.quote: to sound three times (growing weaker and fainter each time) as a threefold warning before the person expires. Along the Glamorganshire coast, the cyhyraeth is said to be heard before a shipwreck, accompanied by a corpse-light.

claims.statement: Like the Irish banshee and Scottish Cailleach, related to the Gwrach y Rhibyn; sounds for Welsh natives dying far from home.
claims.statement_id: Seperti banshee Irlandia dan Cailleach Skotlandia, berkerabat dengan Gwrach y Rhibyn; meratap bagi orang Wales yang mati di perantauan.
claims.quote: Like the Irish banshee and the Scottish Cailleach, to which the cyhyraeth and the Gwrach y Rhibyn are closely related, the cyhyraeth also sounds for Welsh natives dying far from home.

claims.statement: Etymology: cyhyr possibly from oer 'cold'; aeth meaning pain, woe, grief, fear.
claims.statement_id: Asal nama: cyhyr mungkin dari oer (dingin); aeth berarti sakit, duka, takut.
claims.quote: An alternative possibility is that cyhyr is from cyoer, from oer "cold", with the last element being the noun aeth meaning "pain", "woe", "grief", "fear".

claims.statement: The cyhyraeth legend is sometimes conflated with the Gwrach y Rhibyn (Hag of the Mist).
claims.statement_id: Kisah cyhyraeth kadang dicampur dengan Gwrach y Rhibyn (Hag of the Mist).
claims.quote: The legend of the cyhyraeth is sometimes conflated with tales of the Gwrach-y-Rhibyn

claims.statement: Spirits of Welsh mythology with a bodiless voice heard before a death.
claims.statement_id: Roh mitologi Welsh dengan suara tanpa tubuh sebelum kematian.
claims.quote: sind Geister der walisischen Mythologie mit einer körperlosen Stimme, die vor dem Tod eines Menschen zu hören sind.

claims.statement: Like the Cailleach and Banshee, Gwrach and Cyhyraeth lament countrymen dying abroad.
claims.statement_id: Seperti Cailleach dan Banshee, Gwrach dan Cyhyraeth meratapi orang sebangsa yang mati di negeri asing.
claims.quote: Wie die schottischen Cailleach und die irischen Banshee klagen Gwrach und Cyhyraeth auch über den Tod von Landsleuten in der Fremde.

claims.statement: Also cyoeraeth or cyheuraeth; probably from cyhyr 'muscle, sinew, flesh' + -aeth.
claims.statement_id: Juga cyoeraeth atau cyheuraeth; kemungkinan dari cyhyr (otot, urat, daging) + -aeth.
claims.quote: auch cyoeraeth oder cyheuraeth, wahrscheinlich vom Nomen: cyhyr „Muskel, Sehne, Fleisch“ + Endung -aeth

claims.statement: A hairy supernatural being of Isle of Man folklore, a fairy (Manx ferrishyn) helping humans like brownies of Scotland and England.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk gaib berbulu folklor Pulau Man (Isle of Man), sejenis peri (Manx: ferrishyn), membantu manusia seperti brownie di Skotlandia (Scotland) dan Inggris (England).
claims.quote: in the folklore of the Isle of Man, is a hairy supernatural creature, a sort of sprite or fairy (Manx: ferrishyn ), often carrying out chores to help humans, like the brownies of the larger areas of Scotland and England.

claims.statement: Joseph Train and J. F. Campbell glossed the name 'the hairy one'.
claims.statement_id: Joseph Train dan J. F. Campbell mengartikan nama itu "yang berbulu".
claims.quote: Fenodyree has also been glossed simply as "the hairy one" or "something hairy" in Manx by Joseph Train and J. F. Campbell after him.

claims.statement: Carries stone blocks and mows grass at great speed; nicknamed yn foldyr gastey.
claims.statement_id: Mengangkut balok batu dan memotong rumput sangat cepat; dijuluki yn foldyr gastey.
claims.quote: performing arduous tasks such as transporting great blocks of stone, or clipping meadow grass with stupendous speed. For his talent in the grass-cutting skill, he has earned the nickname yn foldyr gastey or "the nimble mower"

claims.statement: A gift of clothing drives it away.
claims.statement_id: Hadiah pakaian mengusirnya.
claims.quote: On the other hand, a gift of clothing would drive the creature away, as attested in several tales.

claims.statement: Some writers call it a giant stronger than any man; I. H. Leney says it was two feet tall.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian penulis menyebutnya raksasa yang lebih kuat dari manusia; I. H. Leney menyebut tingginya dua kaki.
claims.quote: Some writers suggest it was a "giant", or "big and shaggy, with fiery eyes, and stronger than any man", but I. H. Leney (Mrs. J. W. Russell) explains it measured two feet in height

claims.statement: A former Knight of the Fairy Court punished with a satyr-like form for loving a Glen Aldyn girl and missing the harvest festival.
claims.statement_id: Mantan ksatria Istana Peri (Knight of the Fairy Court) dihukum menjadi mirip satir karena mencintai gadis Glen Aldyn dan melewatkan pesta panen.
claims.quote: He was transformed into a grotesque satyr-like appearance as punishment, after falling in love with a human girl from Glen Aldyn and skipping attendance of the royal high festivities of the harvest

claims.statement: The Fynoderee of Gordon was published by Sophia Morrison in 1911.
claims.statement_id: The Fynoderee of Gordon diterbitkan Sophia Morrison pada 1911.
claims.quote: A version that collates several of the fairy's labor is "The Fynoderee of Gordon", published in 1911 by Sophia Morrison.

claims.statement: Other names: Phynodderee, Phynnodderee, Fynnoderee, Yn Foldyr Gastey ('the nimble mower').
claims.statement_id: Nama lain: Phynodderee, Phynnodderee, Fynnoderee, Yn Foldyr Gastey (si pemotong rumput gesit).
claims.quote: Alternative Namen und Schreibweisen sind Fendodyree, Phynodderee, Phynnodderee, Fynnoderee oder sogar Yn Foldyr Gastey, was so viel heißt wie „der flinke Mäher“.

claims.statement: Per the de article (Sage), one tried to carry water in a sieve.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel de (Sage), seorang fenodyree pernah mencoba mengangkut air dengan saringan.
claims.quote: Dieser Mangel zeigt sich in der Sage, dass einer von ihnen einmal versucht haben soll, Wasser in einem Sieb zu transportieren.

claims.statement: Grimalkin or greymalkin, an archaic term for a cat.
claims.statement_id: Grimalkin atau greymalkin, istilah kuno untuk kucing.
claims.quote: A grimalkin, also known as a greymalkin, is an archaic term for a cat.

claims.statement: Scottish legend: a fairy cat dwelling in the Highlands.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Skotlandia (Scottish, Skotlandia): kucing peri yang tinggal di dataran tinggi (Highlands).
claims.quote: Scottish legend makes reference to the grimalkin as a faery cat that dwells in the highlands.

claims.statement: Associated with the devil and witchcraft; women tried as witches in the 16th, 17th, 18th centuries accused of a grimalkin familiar.
claims.statement_id: Dikaitkan dengan iblis dan sihir; perempuan terdakwa penyihir abad ke-16, 17, 18 dituduh memiliki familiar grimalkin.
claims.quote: During the early modern period, the name grimalkin – and cats in general – became associated with the devil and witchcraft. Women tried as witches in the 16th, 17th and 18th centuries were often accused of having a familiar, frequently a grimalkin.

claims.statement: In Shakespeare's Macbeth, Act 1, Scene 1, the First Witch: I come, Graymalkin.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Macbeth (Shakespeare), Babak (Act) 1 Adegan (Scene) 1, Penyihir Pertama (First Witch): I come, Graymalkin.
claims.quote: In Macbeth, Act 1, Scene 1, the First Witch says, "I come, Graymalkin" to her familiar (Shakespeare 1.1.8).

claims.statement: In Scottish folklore (Skotlân), a mythical cat-shaped being of the Highlands (Heechlannen); tales date at least to the Middle Ages (Midsiuwen).
claims.statement_id: Dalam folklor Skotlandia (Skotlân), makhluk mitos berwujud kucing di Highlands (Heechlannen); kisahnya setidaknya dari Abad Pertengahan (Midsiuwen, Middle Ages).
claims.quote: Yn 'e folkloare fan Skotlân wurdt de term grimalkin spesifyk brûkt foar in type mytysk wêzen yn 'e foarm fan in kat. Sokke grimalkins soene yn 'e Skotske Heechlannen libje. Folksferhalen oer sokke katten geane teminsten tebek oant yn 'e Midsiuwen.

claims.statement: From grey + malkin, from a pet form of the female name Maud.
claims.statement_id: Dari grey (kelabu) + malkin, dari bentuk panggilan nama perempuan Maud.
claims.quote: The term stems from "grey" (the colour) plus "malkin", an archaic term with several meanings (a low class woman, a weakling, a mop, or a name) derived from a hypocoristic form of the female name Maud.

claims.statement: In 1606 William Shakespeare included the cat Grimalkin in his tragedy Macbeth.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1606 William Shakespeare memasukkan kucing Grimalkin dalam tragedi Macbeth.
claims.quote: Yn 1606 naam de Ingelske toanielskriuwer William Shakespeare yn syn trageedzje Macbeth

claims.statement: Roger Zelazny's novel A Night in the Lonesome October (1993): a witch's cat named Graymalk.
claims.statement_id: Novel Roger Zelazny A Night in the Lonesome October (1993): kucing penyihir bernama Graymalk.
claims.quote: In Roger Zelazny's fantasy novel A Night in the Lonesome October (1993), "Graymalk" is the name of a cat owned by a witch, possibly in reference to Macbeth.

claims.statement: Habetrot (Habitrot, Habtrot, Habbitrot), a folklore figure of the Border counties of Northern England and Lowland Scotland, linked with spinning.
claims.statement_id: Habetrot (Habitrot, Habtrot, Habbitrot), tokoh folklor daerah perbatasan (Border) Inggris Utara (Northern England) dan Dataran Rendah Skotlandia (Lowland Scotland), terkait pemintalan.
claims.quote: Habetrot (Habitrot, Habtrot and Habbitrot) is a figure in folklore of the Border counties of Northern England and Lowland Scotland, associated with spinning and the spinning wheel.

claims.statement: A Selkirkshire tale of type ATU 501 (The Three Old Spinning Women); an old deformed woman living underground with other spinners.
claims.statement_id: Dongeng Selkirkshire, tipe ATU 501 (The Three Old Spinning Women); perempuan tua cacat yang tinggal di bawah tanah bersama pemintal lain.
claims.quote: Habetrot appears in a Selkirkshire folktale which is a variant of the Aarne–Thompson–Uther Index tale type ATU 501, "The Three Old Spinning Women". She is an old, deformed woman who lives underground with a group of other spinsters

claims.statement: Scantlie Mab; Habetrot spun for a girl and convinced her husband she should never spin again.
claims.statement_id: Scantlie Mab; Habetrot memintal untuk seorang gadis lalu meyakinkan suaminya agar ia tak memintal lagi.
claims.quote: The only other named spinster is Scantlie Mab. Habetrot spun yarn for a local girl and then convinced the girl's new husband that she should never spin again.

claims.statement: Similar tales in Germany (The Three Spinners) and Norway (The Three Aunts).
claims.statement_id: Kisah serupa di Jerman (Germany, The Three Spinners) dan Norwegia (Norway, The Three Aunts).
claims.quote: Similar tales appear in countries such as Germany (such as The Three Spinners) and Norway (The Three Aunts).

claims.statement: it article: Scantlie Mab; Habetrot spun for a local girl.
claims.statement_id: Artikel it: Scantlie Mab; Habetrot memintal untuk gadis setempat (Habetrot filava).
claims.quote: L'unica altra filatrice nominata è Scantlie Mab. Habetrot filava il filato per una ragazza del posto e poi convinse il nuovo marito della ragazza che non avrebbe mai più dovuto filare.

claims.statement: Grave-merels from unchristened graves is relieved only by a linen sack spun by Habetrot (Border lore).
claims.statement_id: Penyakit grave-merels dari makam bayi tak dibaptis hanya reda dengan karung linen yang dipintal Habetrot (Border).
claims.quote: The only way to relieve this was for the afflicted to wear a sack made from linen grown in a field using manure from a farmyard that has not been disturbed for forty years, spun by Habetrot

claims.statement: Katie King, a spirit of 1870s Spiritualist séances; appeared 1871–1874 with Florence Cook in London, then 1874–1875 in New York with Jennie and Nelson Holmes; mid-1870s controversy.
claims.statement_id: Katie King, roh dalam seans kaum Spiritualis (Spiritualists) tahun 1870-an; muncul 1871–1874 pada Florence Cook di London (Inggris), lalu 1874–1875 di New York pada Jennie dan Nelson Holmes; kontroversi pertengahan 1870-an.
claims.quote: The spirit was said to have appeared first between 1871 and 1874 in séances conducted by Florence Cook in London, and later in 1874–1875 in New York in séances held by the mediums Jennie Holmes and her husband Nelson Holmes.

claims.statement: John King, Katie King's father, claimed to be the spirit of the buccaneer Henry Morgan; a spirit control.
claims.statement_id: John King, ayah Katie King, mengaku roh bajak laut Henry Morgan; roh pengendali (spirit control).
claims.quote: John King claimed to be the spirit of Henry Morgan, the buccaneer (Doyle 1926: volume 1, 241, 277).

claims.statement: At Hackney, 9 December 1873, lawyer William Volckman attended Cook's séance and accused the spirit of being Cook.
claims.statement_id: Di Hackney, 9 Desember 1873, pengacara William Volckman menghadiri seans Cook dan menuduh roh itu Cook yang menyamar.
claims.quote: At Hackney on 9 December 1873, lawyer William Volckman attended a séance held by Florence Cook, during which Katie King materialized and, as was customary, held the hands of participants.

claims.statement: Sir William Crookes, scientist, investigated Spiritualist mediums 1871–1874.
claims.statement_id: Sir William Crookes, ilmuwan, meneliti fenomena medium Spiritualis 1871–1874.
claims.quote: Between 1871 and 1874, Sir William Crookes investigated the preternatural phenomena produced by Spiritualist mediums.

claims.statement: Eliza White claimed to have masqueraded as Katie; her face matched the Holmeses' photographs.
claims.statement_id: Eliza White mengaku menyamar sebagai Katie; wajahnya cocok dengan foto keluarga Holmes.
claims.quote: a woman named Eliza White stepped forward and claimed to have masqueraded as Katie. White's face matched that of "Katie King" in photographs sold by the Holmeses and their agents.

claims.statement: Name given by Florence Cook to a supposed ectoplasm materialisation in human form.
claims.statement_id: Nama dari Florence Cook untuk dugaan materialisasi ektoplasma berwujud manusia.
claims.quote: Katie King es el nombre dado por la espiritista Florence Cook a una supuesta materialización de un ectoplasma que en sus apariciones tomaba forma humana.

claims.statement: Per the es article, William Crookes photographed her, obtaining 44 photographs.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel es, William Crookes memotretnya dan memperoleh 44 foto.
claims.quote: La aparición andaba y hablaba con libertad, incluso William Crookes pudo fotografiarla en diferentes ocasiones, consiguiendo 44 fotografías.

claims.statement: King Goldemar (Goldmar, Vollmar, Volmar), Germanic dwarf/kobold; king of the dwarfs by the Middle Ages in German belief; brothers Alberich (Elberich) and Elbegast; Ludwig Uhland's Der junge König und die Schäferin.
claims.statement_id: Raja Goldemar (Goldmar, Vollmar, Volmar), kurcaci/kobold Jermanik; raja kurcaci Abad Pertengahan (Middle Ages) dalam kepercayaan Jerman (German); saudaranya Alberich (Elberich) dan Elbegast; Der junge König und die Schäferin karya Ludwig Uhland.
claims.quote: is a dwarf or kobold from Germanic mythology and folklore. By the Middle Ages, Goldemar had become the king of the dwarfs in German belief.

claims.statement: Fragments of Albrecht von Kemenaten's epic Goldemar: Dietrich meets the dwarf king.
claims.statement_id: Penggalan puisi epik Goldemar karya Albrecht von Kemenaten: pertemuan Dietrich dengan raja kurcaci.
claims.quote: Fragments of an epic poem by Albrecht von Kemenaten called Goldemar survive. The poem tells of Dietrich's encounter with the dwarf king.

claims.statement: Per Thomas Keightley (1850), a kobold living with Neveling von Hardenberg at Castle Hardenstein on the Ruhr River; skilled harpist.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Thomas Keightley (1850), kobold yang tinggal bersama Neveling von Hardenberg di Kastel (Castle) Hardenstein, Sungai (River) Ruhr; pandai bermain harpa.
claims.quote: Goldemar lived with Neveling von Hardenberg at Castle Hardenstein at the Ruhr River. Goldemar frequently interacted with mortals. He called Neveling his "brother-in-law" and often slept in the same bed with him. He skillfully played the harp

claims.statement: Refused to be seen but could be felt; hands like a frog's (Keightley).
claims.statement_id: Menolak dilihat tetapi boleh diraba; tangannya seperti katak (Keightley).
claims.quote: The spirit refused to be seen, but he would allow mortals to feel him; Keightley says that "[h]is hands were thin like those of a frog, cold and soft to the feel."

claims.statement: Goldemar cut up, cooked and ate the man who strewed ashes, then left; the house would be unlucky.
claims.statement_id: Goldemar mencincang, memasak dan memakan orang yang menabur abu, lalu pergi; rumah akan sial.
claims.quote: Goldemar cut the man to pieces, put them on the fire to roast, and put the head and legs in a pot to boil. He then took the cooked meat to his chambers and ate it with glee. The next day, Goldemar was gone.

claims.statement: it article: lived with Neveling von Hardenberg at Hardenstein castle on the Ruhr.
claims.statement_id: Artikel it: tinggal bersama Neveling von Hardenberg di kastel Hardenstein, Ruhr.
claims.quote: Viveva con Neveling von Hardenberg al castello Hardenstein sul fiume Ruhr. Interagiva frequentemente coi mortali.

claims.statement: A water dragon of Sussex dialect, England, in knuckerholes; from Old English nicor, water monster, used in Beowulf.
claims.statement_id: Naga air dialek Sussex, Inggris (England), di knuckerhole; dari kata Inggris Kuno (Old English) nicor, monster air, dalam Beowulf.
claims.quote: Knucker is a dialect word for a sort of water dragon, living in knuckerholes in Sussex, England. The word comes from the Old English nicor which means "water monster" and is used in the poem Beowulf. It may also be related to the word "nixie"

claims.statement: The knucker has wings and is sometimes described as a sea serpent.
claims.statement_id: Knucker bersayap, kadang digambarkan sebagai ular laut.
claims.quote: The knucker is said to have wings, and is sometimes described as a sea serpent.

claims.statement: A knight-errant slew it at the King of Sussex's offer; the Slayer's Slab in Lyminster church; it ate livestock and villagers.
claims.statement_id: Ksatria pengembara membunuhnya atas janji Raja Sussex; Slayer's Slab di gereja Lyminster; knucker memangsa ternak dan penduduk.
claims.quote: One version has the dragon slain by a knight-errant after the king of Sussex offered his daughter's hand in marriage to whoever rid them of the beast. Legend says that after marrying the princess, the knight settled in Lyminster and his gravestone, the Slayer's Slab, can be seen in Lyminster church.

claims.statement: Jim Pulk or Jim Puttock, for the Mayor of Arundel's reward, killed the dragon with a giant poisoned pie and beheaded it; brought on a horse and cart.
claims.statement_id: Jim Pulk atau Jim Puttock, hadiah Wali Kota (Mayor) Arundel, membunuh naga dengan pai beracun raksasa dan memenggal kepalanya; dibawa dengan kereta kuda.
claims.quote: An alternative legend has the dragon outwitted by a local farmer's boy, called Jim Pulk or Jim Puttock, said in some versions to be from Wick, after the Mayor of Arundel offered a reward. He killed the dragon by cooking it a giant poisoned pie

claims.statement: Knuckerholes at Binsted, Lyminster, Lancing, Shoreham, Worthing; deep round bottomless pools.
claims.statement_id: Knuckerhole di Binsted, Lyminster, Lancing, Shoreham, Worthing; kolam bundar dalam tak berdasar.
claims.quote: It was believed that knuckers could be found at knuckerholes in various places in Sussex, including Binsted, Lyminster, Lancing, Shoreham and Worthing. A knucker hole is a very deep round pool, which is considered to be infinitely deep.

claims.statement: de article: a serpentine water dragon of Sussex; constant-temperature chalk spring pools that mist in frost.
claims.statement_id: Artikel de: naga air mirip ular dari Sussex; kolam mata air kapur bersuhu tetap, berkabut saat beku.
claims.quote: Der Knucker ist ein schlangenartiger Wasserdrache aus Sagen in der südenglischen Grafschaft Sussex.

claims.statement: Thin mist over the water in frost helped give rise to the knucker legends.
claims.statement_id: Kabut tipis di atas air saat udara beku turut melahirkan legenda knucker.
claims.quote: Bei frostigen Lufttemperaturen bildet sich dünner Nebel über dem Wasser, was zur Legendenbildung um die Knucker beigetragen hat.

claims.statement: Lubber fiend (Lob, lubberkin, lurdane, Lob Lie-By-The-Fire), English folklore; like the brownie/Urisk of Scotland, hob, Slavic domovoi, Scandinavian tomte; Robin Goodfellow; mentioned by John Milton in L'Allegro.
claims.statement_id: Lubber fiend (Lob, lubberkin, lurdane, Lob Lie-By-The-Fire), folklor Inggris (English); mirip brownie/Urisk Skotlandia, hob, domovoi Slavia, tomte Skandinavia; Robin Goodfellow; disebut John Milton dalam L'Allegro.
claims.quote: is a legendary creature of English folklore that is similar to the "brownie" (or "Urisk") of Scotland and northern England, the "hob" of northern England and the Scottish Borders, the Slavic "domovoi" and Scandinavian "tomte". It has been related also to Robin Goodfellow, and Hobgoblins. It is best known for being mentioned by John Milton in his pastoral poem, "L'Allegro".

claims.statement: Large hairy tailed man doing housework for milk and a place by the fire.
claims.statement_id: Lelaki besar berbulu berekor, bekerja demi susu dan tempat di depan perapian.
claims.quote: The lubberkin is typically described as a large, hairy man with a tail who performs housework in exchange for a saucer of milk and a place in front of the fire.

claims.statement: Giant son of a witch and the Devil; the abbey lubber, a minor demon of abbeys.
claims.statement_id: Putra raksasa penyihir dan Iblis (Devil); abbey lubber setan kecil di biara.
claims.quote: One story claims he is the giant son of a witch and the Devil. The abbey lubber is a minor demon that haunts the wine cellars and kitchens of abbeys, tempting the monks into drunkenness, gluttony and lasciviousness.

claims.statement: In The Red Axe by S. R. Crockett (1900).
claims.statement_id: Dalam The Red Axe karya S. R. Crockett (1900).
claims.quote: The lubber fiend appears also in The Red Axe by S. R. Crockett (1900): That fool, Jan Lubber Fiend, will ever be at his tricks.

claims.statement: Edward Thomas's poem Lob; Lob Lie-By-The-Fire (Juliana H. Ewing); Dear Brutus (J. M. Barrie).
claims.statement_id: Puisi Lob karya Edward Thomas; Lob Lie-By-The-Fire (Juliana H. Ewing); Dear Brutus (J. M. Barrie).
claims.quote: Lob is the title of a poem by Edward Thomas. It also appears in Lob Lie-By-The-Fire by Juliana H. Ewing, Troll Fell by Katherine Langrish, Abbeychurch by Charlotte M. Yonge and Dear Brutus by J. M. Barrie

claims.statement: fr article: the Abbey Lubber is a minor demon of abbey wine cellars and kitchens; Friar Rush.
claims.statement_id: Artikel fr: Abbey Lubber setan kecil penghuni gudang anggur dan dapur biara; Friar Rush.
claims.quote: L'Abbey Lubber est un démon mineur qui hante les caves à vin et les cuisines des abbayes

claims.statement: A lubberkin in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt as a protective household spirit.
claims.statement_id: Lubberkin dalam The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt sebagai roh pelindung rumah.
claims.quote: A creature called a lubberkin appears in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, in which it is a type of protective household spirit

claims.statement: Moddey Dhoo, a phantom black dog of Manx folklore haunting Peel Castle on the Isle of Man.
claims.statement_id: Moddey Dhoo, anjing hitam (black dog) hantu folklor Manx, menghantui Kastel Peel (Peel Castle) di Pulau Man (Isle of Man).
claims.quote: meaning "black dog" in Manx) is a phantom black dog in Manx folklore that reputedly haunted Peel Castle on the west coast of the Isle of Man.

claims.statement: Mis-transcribed Mauthe Doog by an 18th-century source.
claims.statement_id: Salah tulis menjadi Mauthe Doog oleh sumber abad ke-18.
claims.quote: The Manx name Moddey Dhoo was mis-transcribed as Mauthe Doog (/ˈmɔːðə doʊɡ/) by an influential 18th-Century English-speaking folklore source

claims.statement: Per George Waldron, English topographer and poet: a large curly black spaniel in Peel Castle's guard-chamber.
claims.statement_id: Menurut George Waldron, penyair dan topografer Inggris (English): spaniel hitam besar berbulu keriting di ruang jaga Kastel Peel.
claims.quote: in the shape of a large black spaniel with curled shaggy hair, was used to haunt Peel Castle; and has been frequently seen in every room, but particularly in the guard-chamber

claims.statement: Came from the passage at dusk, returned at dawn.
claims.statement_id: Datang dari lorong saat senja, kembali saat fajar.
claims.quote: the Mauthe Doog was always seen to come from that passage at the close of day, and return to it again as soon as the morning dawned

claims.statement: The drunken guard returned terrified and died three days later; the passage was sealed.
claims.statement_id: Penjaga mabuk kembali ketakutan dan mati tiga hari kemudian; lorong ditutup.
claims.quote: Some noises were heard, the adventurer returned to the guard-room, ghastly frightened, unable to share the story of what he had seen, and died three days later.

claims.statement: Sir Walter Scott in Peveril of the Peak (1823).
claims.statement_id: Sir Walter Scott dalam Peveril of the Peak (1823).
claims.quote: The dog was made known to the world at large when Sir Walter Scott introduced the "Manthe Dog -- a fiend, or demon, in the shape of a large, shaggy, black mastiff" in Peveril of the Peak (1823)

claims.statement: Similar to the yeth hound of Devon and gwyllgi of Wales; nl article: incident in 1666.
claims.statement_id: Mirip yeth hound Devon dan gwyllgi Wales; artikel nl: kejadian 1666.
claims.quote: De beschrijvingen van de Moddey Dhoo vertonen overeenkomsten met vergelijkbare verhalen over hellehonden die tot de overleveringen van de Britse Eilanden behoren, waaronder de yeth hound uit Devon en de gwyllgi uit Wales.

claims.statement: The incident Waldron recorded took place in 1666, after the English Civil War.
claims.statement_id: Insiden yang dicatat Waldron terjadi pada 1666, setelah Perang Saudara Inggris.
claims.quote: het door hem beschreven incident zou zich echter in 1666 hebben voorgedaan, kort na de Engelse Burgeroorlog

claims.statement: Nicneven, Nicnevin, Nicnevan: witch or fairy queen of Scottish folklore, often equated with the Gyre-Carling or Hecate.
claims.statement_id: Nicneven, Nicnevin, Nicnevan: penyihir atau ratu peri folklor Skotlandia (Scottish), sering disamakan dengan Gyre-Carling atau Hecate.
claims.quote: Nicneven, Nicnevin or Nicnevan is a witch or fairy queen from Scottish folklore. She is often said to be the same figure as the Gyre-Carling or Hecate, but some scholars disagree with this.

claims.statement: Name from Scottish Gaelic Neachneohain or NicNaoimhein, or the Irish war goddess Neamhain.
claims.statement_id: Nama dari Gaelik Skotlandia (Scottish Gaelic) Neachneohain atau NicNaoimhein, atau dewi perang Irlandia (Irish) Neamhain.
claims.quote: The name may derive from a Scottish Gaelic surname Neachneohain, meaning "daughter(s) of the divine", and/or "daughter(s) of Scathach", or NicNaoimhein, meaning "daughter of the little saint". Other theories propose that the name derives from the Irish war goddess Neamhain

claims.statement: First mentioned by Alexander Montgomerie c. 1580; court poets of King James VI with Patrick Hume of Polwarth (Polwart); a flyting.
claims.statement_id: Disebut pertama oleh Alexander Montgomerie sekitar 1580; penyair istana Raja (King) James VI bersama Patrick Hume dari (of) Polwarth (Polwart); flyting.
claims.quote: The first known mention of Nicneven was by Alexander Montgomerie around 1580. Montgomerie and Patrick Hume of Polwarth were two court poets under King James VI of Scotland.

claims.statement: The infant Polwart is given to Nicneven and her witches, dedicated to Hecate and Pluto.
claims.statement_id: Bayi Polwart diserahkan kepada Nicneven dan penyihirnya, dipersembahkan kepada Hecate dan Pluto.
claims.quote: The infant Polwart is found by the Weird Sisters and then passed on to Nicneven and her group of nymphs or witches, who dedicate him to Hecatus (Hecate) and Pluto in an unholy ritual.

claims.statement: Per Robert Cromek: mothers frighten children with McNeven (Gyre Carline); long grey mantle, wand turning water to rock.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Robert Cromek: para ibu menakuti anak dengan McNeven (Gyre Carline); mantel kelabu panjang, tongkat pengubah air jadi batu.
claims.quote: mothers frequently frighten their children by threatening to give them to McNeven, or the Gyre Carline. She is described as wearing a long gray mantle, and carrying a wand, which, like the miraculous rod of Moses, could convert water into rocks and sea into solid land.

claims.statement: John Leyden (1801): Nicneven a popular name of the gyre-carlin, Queen of Fairies.
claims.statement_id: John Leyden (1801): Nicneven nama populer gyre-carlin, Ratu Peri (Queen of Fairies).
claims.quote: In 1801, John Leyden wrote that Nicneven was one of the "popular appellations" of "the gyre-carlin, the Queen of Fairies, the great hag, Hecate, or mother-witch of the peasants".

claims.statement: Debated whether the name referred to a real woman or a goddess.
claims.statement_id: Diperdebatkan apakah nama itu merujuk pada perempuan nyata atau dewi.
claims.quote: Se debate si este nombre se refería originalmente a una mujer real o a una diosa mitológica.

claims.statement: Pearlin Jean, a ghost of the Allanbank Courtyard, Allanton, Berwickshire, Scotland; former dower house of Blackadder House.
claims.statement_id: Pearlin Jean, hantu di halaman Allanbank (Allanbank Courtyard), Allanton, Berwickshire, Skotlandia (Scotland); bekas rumah janda tanah Blackadder House.
claims.quote: Pearlin Jean is the name given to a ghost, who purportedly haunts the Allanbank Courtyard, situated in Allanton, Berwickshire, Scotland. The courtyard was previously the site of a dower house called Allanbank of the country estate of the now demolished Blackadder House.

claims.statement: Named from the pearlin lace covering her.
claims.statement_id: Nama dari renda (lace) pearlin yang menutupinya.
claims.quote: The ghost's name is derived from the eye-witness' claim that she is seen covered in the similarly named lace

claims.statement: Jean stepped in front of Stewart's carriage and was killed; last words: I'll be in Scotland before you; from Paris.
claims.statement_id: Jean menghadang kereta Stewart dan tewas dilindas; kata terakhir: I'll be in Scotland before you; berasal dari Paris.
claims.quote: Jean attempted to physically stop Stewart from leaving her by stepping out in front of his carriage. He ordered his driver to carry on regardless, and the woman fell. The wheels of the carriage then ran over her forehead, killing her.

claims.statement: Stewart saw her atop the entrance covered in blood, before 1697.
claims.statement_id: Stewart melihatnya di atas gerbang berlumur darah, sebelum 1697.
claims.quote: he saw his ex-lover sitting on top of the entrance to the estate, with blood covering her head and shoulders. This first sighting was at least prior to 1697.

claims.statement: The ghost slammed doors and opened windows; later a skeleton in Pearlin lace; seven ministers failed to exorcise it.
claims.statement_id: Hantu membanting pintu, membuka jendela; kemudian berwujud kerangka berbalut renda Pearlin; tujuh pendeta gagal mengusirnya.
claims.quote: The ghost was said to slam doors, open windows and walk throughout the house at all times of the day and night. As time progressed, Pearlin Jean's ghostly figure became that of a skeleton in Pearlin lace

claims.statement: Thomas Blackadder was frightened in the 18th century; footsteps in 1790; 19th-century song.
claims.statement_id: Thomas Blackadder ketakutan pada abad ke-18; 1790 suara langkah kaki; lagu abad ke-19.
claims.quote: In the 1700s, Thomas Blackadder was said to be infatuated with the figure of Pearlin Jean, and went to meet her in the courtyard. As soon as he realised the nature of the woman, he became incredibly frightened.

claims.statement: Lover of Sir Robert Stewart, made a Baronet in 1684.
claims.statement_id: Kekasih Sir Robert Stewart, diangkat Baronet (baronet) pada 1684.
claims.quote: Según la leyenda, fue amante de Sir Robert Stewart (quien fue nombrado baronet en 1684) y monja de la caridad que no estaba confinada a un claustro.

claims.statement: Pictish Beast (Pictish Dragon, Pictish Elephant): a stylised animal of the early medieval Picts of Scotland, on Pictish stones.
claims.statement_id: Pictish Beast (Pictish Dragon, Pictish Elephant): gambaran hewan khas budaya Pikt (Picts) Skotlandia (Scotland) awal Abad Pertengahan, pada batu Pikt (Pictish stones).
claims.quote: is a conventional representation of an animal, distinct to the early medieval culture of the Picts of Scotland. The great majority of surviving examples are on Pictish stones.

claims.statement: The symbol in the Doo Cave at East Wemyss, recorded by Anderson in 1881: long jaws, crest, scroll-like feet.
claims.statement_id: Simbol di Doo Cave, East Wemyss, dicatat Anderson pada 1881: rahang panjang, jambul, kaki bergulung.
claims.quote: One omission from Stuart's plate is the symbol in the Doo Cave at East Wemyss, recorded by Anderson in 1881. Anderson described it as "the symbolic animal, with the long jaws and the crest and the scroll-like feet".

claims.statement: Jill Harden: the figure is swimming; porpoise, dolphin or mythical creature?
claims.statement_id: Jill Harden: sosok ini berenang; pesut, lumba-lumba, atau makhluk mitos?
claims.quote: This intriguing figure is clearly swimming. Is it a porpoise, a dolphin or a creature of myth?

claims.statement: Other identifications: elephant, kelpie (each uisge), seahorse.
claims.statement_id: Identifikasi lain: gajah, kelpie (each uisge), kuda laut.
claims.quote: Other suggested identifications of the Pictish beast have included an elephant, a kelpie (or each uisge), and a seahorse.

claims.statement: 7th to 9th centuries; 29 times on Class I stones, 25 on Class II, five on cave walls; animal or chimera unclear.
claims.statement_id: Abad ke-7 hingga ke-9; 29 kali pada batu Kelas (Klasse) I, 25 kali Kelas II, lima kali di dinding gua; hewan atau chimera belum jelas.
claims.quote: Die Figuren entstanden zwischen dem 7. und 9. Jahrhundert. Ob ein Tier oder eine Chimäre dargestellt wird, ist ungeklärt. Es ist eines der häufigsten Symbole im piktischen Repertoire und kommt 29 Mal auf Steinen der Klasse I, 25 Mal auf Steinen der Klasse II und fünf Mal auf Höhlenwänden vor.

claims.statement: Features: long beak-like snout, curled limb ends, lappet, hanging tail; appears swimming.
claims.statement_id: Ciri: moncong panjang seperti paruh, ujung kaki menggulung, jambul, ekor menggantung; tampak berenang.
claims.quote: Charakteristisch sind die lange, schnabelartige Schnauze, die rundlichen, aufgerollten Enden der Gliedmaßen

claims.statement: Seonaidh (Shony, Shoney), a water spirit of Lewis, Scotland, per Martin Martin.
claims.statement_id: Seonaidh (dibakukan dalam bahasa Inggris: Shony, Shoney), roh air di Lewis, Skotlandia (Scotland), menurut Martin Martin.
claims.quote: The Seonaidh (anglicised Shony or Shoney) was a water spirit in Lewis, according to Martin Martin.

claims.statement: Dwelly: seonadh = augury, sorcery, Druidism; Lewis folk met at the church of St. Mulway (Mael rubha), malt brewed into ale.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Dwelly: seonadh = tenung, sihir, Druidisme; penduduk Lewis berkumpul di gereja St. Mulway (Mael rubha), malt diseduh menjadi ale.
claims.quote: They came to the church of St. Mulway (Mael rubha ), each man carrying his own provisions. Every family gave a pock (bag) of malt, and the whole was brewed into ale.

claims.statement: Ale offered to Seonaidh for seaweed to enrich the ground.
claims.statement_id: Persembahan ale kepada Seonaidh untuk rumput laut penyubur tanah.
claims.quote: I give thee this cup of ale, hoping that thou wilt be so good as to send us plenty of seaware [seaweed used as a fertilizer] for enriching our ground during the coming year.

claims.statement: The ale thrown into the sea in a night ceremony.
claims.statement_id: Ale dilempar ke laut dalam upacara malam.
claims.quote: He then threw the ale into the sea, in a ceremony performed at night.

claims.statement: Seonaidh was likely once a god whose cult was Christianised.
claims.statement_id: Seonaidh mungkin semula dewa yang pemujaannya dikristenkan.
claims.quote: It seems likely that Seonaidh was originally some kind of god, whose worship had been lightly Christianised by the addition of various church features.

claims.statement: Seonaidh, Scottish Gaelic for Johnny, may refer to one of the Saints John.
claims.statement_id: Seonaidh bentuk Gaelik Skotlandia (Scottish Gaelic) untuk Johnny, mungkin merujuk Santo Yohanes (Saints John).
claims.quote: However, it is also possible that Seonaidh , the Scottish Gaelic form of the English Johnny, may also be a reference to one of the Saints John.

claims.statement: tr article: the people of Lewis offered ale to this water spirit for good harvests.
claims.statement_id: Artikel tr: penduduk Lewis mempersembahkan ale kepada roh air ini demi panen.
claims.quote: Lewis halkı ekinlerinin çok mahsul vermesi için bu su cinine bir çeşit bira olan ale adarlardı.

claims.statement: Sheka (Cyrillic: Шекә) is a dwarf-like being in Turkic mythology that lives in forests or derelict houses; in the legends it tends to appear in comical situations.
claims.statement_id: Sheka (Sirilik: Шекә) adalah makhluk mirip kurcaci dalam mitologi Turkik yang tinggal di hutan atau rumah terbengkalai; dalam legenda ia cenderung muncul dalam situasi lucu.
claims.quote: Sheka (Cyrillic: Шекә) is a dwarf-like being in the Turkic mythology, that lives in forests or derelict houses. In the legends they tend to appear in comical situations.

claims.statement: In Slavic paganism Sheka is a field spirit: a deformed dwarf with differently coloured eyes and grass instead of hair, appearing at noon or sunset in all-black or all-white clothes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam paganisme Slavia, Sheka adalah roh ladang: kurcaci cacat bermata beda warna dan berambut rumput; muncul tengah hari atau senja dengan pakaian serba hitam atau serba putih.
claims.quote: Sheka in Slavic paganism is field spirit that appears as a deformed dwarf with different coloured eyes and grass instead of hair. It appears either at noon or sunset and wear either all black or all white suits.

claims.statement: In Slavic paganism, according to local beliefs, Sheka leads wandering people astray in a field, gives them diseases or rides them over with horses if they are found asleep; it enjoys pulling the hair of peasants working at midday.
claims.statement_id: Dalam paganisme Slavia, Sheka menurut kepercayaan setempat menyesatkan orang yang mengembara di ladang, menularkan penyakit, atau melindas orang yang tertidur dengan kuda; ia senang menarik rambut petani yang bekerja di siang hari.
claims.quote: Sheka in Slavic paganism is field spirit ... According to local beliefs it leads wandering people in a field astray, give them diseases or ride them over with horses if they are found asleep. It enjoys pulling the hair of peasants working in the midday.

claims.statement: Catalan Wikipedia article: Şekä (Tatar: Şekä or Шекә; Turkish: Çike) is a dwarf-like being of Tatar mythology that lives in forests or abandoned houses.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Wikipedia bahasa Katalan: Şekä (Tatar: Şekä atau Шекә; Turki: Çike) adalah makhluk mirip kurcaci dalam mitologi Tatar yang hidup di hutan atau rumah terbengkalai.
claims.quote: Şekä (del tàtar: Şekä o Шекә, turc: Çike) és un ésser semblant a un nan propi de la mitologia tàtara, que viu als boscos o cases abandonades.

claims.statement: In Slavic paganism, Sheka makes little children get lost in cornfields.
claims.statement_id: Dalam paganisme Slavia, Sheka membuat anak-anak kecil tersesat di ladang jagung (cornfield).
claims.quote: Sheka in Slavic paganism is field spirit ... It also makes little children get lost in cornfields.

claims.statement: In Slavic paganism, if Sheka catches a person it forces him to sing, which lasts for hours.
claims.statement_id: Dalam paganisme Slavia, Sheka memaksa orang yang ditangkapnya bernyanyi selama berjam-jam.
claims.quote: Sheka in Slavic paganism is field spirit ... If it catches a person it forces him to sing, which lasts for hours.

claims.statement: Sihirtia (сихиртя) or Sirtia (сиртя), a mythical people of the tundra before the Nenets; Nenets folklore.
claims.statement_id: Sihirtia (сихиртя) atau Sirtia (сиртя), bangsa mitos tundra sebelum orang Nenets; folklor Nenets.
claims.quote: Sihirtia (Nenets: сихиртя ) or Sirtia (Nenets: сиртя ) were a mythical people who lived in the tundra before the arrival of the Nenets. The name is often encountered in the folklore of the Nenets.

claims.statement: Very short, finely dressed with metal pendants; live in sandy hills; emerge at night or in mist; underground ride dogs and herd mammoths (earth deer).
claims.statement_id: Sangat pendek, berpakaian indah berliontin logam; tinggal di bukit pasir; keluar malam atau saat berkabut; di bawah tanah naik anjing dan menggembala mamut (rusa tanah).
claims.quote: Tall sandy hills served them as homes. They came out to the surface of the tundra at night or in the mist; they lived under the ground, where they traveled on dogs and pastured mammoths ("earth deer").

claims.statement: Sihirtia were skilled smiths and good warriors.
claims.statement_id: Sihirtia pandai besi terampil dan prajurit baik.
claims.quote: Sihirtia were skilled smiths and good warriors.

claims.statement: Meeting a Sihirtia brought bad or good luck; marriages with Nenets.
claims.statement_id: Bertemu Sihirtia membawa sial atau untung; pernikahan dengan orang Nenets.
claims.quote: Meeting a Sihirtia brought either misfortune or good luck. There were cases of marriage between Nenets and Sihirtia.

claims.statement: Possibly features of a real Samoyedic or Paleo-Siberian people of the European and West Siberian tundra in antiquity; Russia.
claims.statement_id: Mungkin ciri bangsa nyata asal Samoyed (Samoyedic) atau Paleo-Siberia (Paleo-Siberian) di tundra Eropa (Europe) dan Siberia Barat (West Siberian) pada zaman kuno; Rusia.
claims.quote: The folklore image of Sihirtia might have mythologically imprinted features of a real people (probably of Samoyedic or Paleo-Siberian origin) who lived in Europe and West Siberian tundra in antiquity.

claims.statement: ru article: a mythical Nenets people living underground and fearing daylight.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ru: bangsa mitos Nenets yang tinggal di bawah tanah dan takut cahaya siang.
claims.quote: в ненецкой мифологии мифический народ, ныне живущий под землёй, боящийся дневного света, обитавший в заполярной тундре до прихода ненцев

claims.statement: Thetis Lake Monster, a legendary creature and hoax of Victoria, British Columbia, Canada, 1972; like the Gill-man of Creature from the Black Lagoon (1954).
claims.statement_id: Monster Danau Thetis (Thetis Lake Monster), makhluk legenda dan tipuan dari Victoria, British Columbia, Kanada (Canada), 1972; mirip Gill-man film Creature from the Black Lagoon (1954).
claims.quote: The Thetis Lake Monster is a legendary creature and admitted hoax of Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. In 1972, two teenage boys claimed to see a monster emerge from Thetis Lake beach.

claims.statement: Victoria Daily Times, 22 August 1972: silvery scaled skin, sharp claws, head spikes.
claims.statement_id: Victoria Daily Times, 22 Agustus (August) 1972: kulit sisik keperakan, cakar tajam, duri di kepala.
claims.quote: On 22 August 1972, the Victoria Daily Times reported that two local teen boys claimed to have seen a creature with "silvery scaled skin, sharp claws, and spikes on its head" while swimming at Thetis Lake beach in the evening.

claims.statement: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police found no evidence.
claims.statement_id: Polisi Berkuda Kerajaan Kanada (Royal Canadian Mounted Police) tidak menemukan bukti.
claims.quote: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police investigated, but could find no evidence.

claims.statement: Daniel Loxton: the description matched the monster of the film Monster From The Surf on local TV.
claims.statement_id: Daniel Loxton: deskripsi sama dengan monster film Monster From The Surf di televisi setempat.
claims.quote: Loxton discovered that the boys description of the scaly monster – which specified a sharply pointed head and large, ear-like gills — exactly matched that of the monster featured in the film Monster From The Surf

claims.statement: fi article: a lizard-man with hooked claws, sharp fins, gills and lungs, webbed hands and feet.
claims.statement_id: Artikel fi: manusia kadal bercakar, bersirip tajam, berinsang dan berparu-paru, tangan dan kaki berselaput.
claims.quote: Sillä väitetään olevan koukkukynnet, viiltävän terävät evät ja sekä kidukset että keuhkot. Hirviöllä sanotaan olevan myös räpylät käsissään ja jaloissaan

claims.statement: A witness admitted to Daniel Loxton the story was fabricated.
claims.statement_id: Saksi mengaku kepada Daniel Loxton bahwa cerita itu dikarang.
claims.quote: However, when writer Daniel Loxton contacted one of the individuals years later, he admitted they had fabricated the story to get attention.

claims.statement: Thunderdell (Welsh: Taranau; Thunderdel, Thunderel, Thundrel, Thunderdale, Thunderbore), a two-headed Cornish giant slain by Jack the Giant-Killer in Tabart's stories.
claims.statement_id: Thunderdell (Welsh: Taranau; Thunderdel, Thunderel, Thundrel, Thunderdale, Thunderbore), raksasa berkepala dua Cornwall dibunuh Jack the Giant-Killer (Jack the Giant Killer) dalam kisah Tabart.
claims.quote: Thunderdell (Welsh: Taranau ), also recorded as Thunderdel, Thunderel, Thundrel, Thunderdale, or Thunderbore, was a two-headed giant of Cornwall slain by Jack the Giant-Killer in the stories of Tabart and others.

claims.statement: In Jack the Giant Killer, Thunderdell first appears crashing a banquet prepared for Jack, chanting "fee fau fum"; Jack defeats and beheads the two-headed giant with a trick involving the house's moat and drawbridge.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Jack the Giant Killer, Thunderdell muncul dengan mengacau perjamuan yang disiapkan untuk Jack sambil menyerukan "fee fau fum"; Jack mengalahkan dan memenggal raksasa berkepala dua itu dengan tipu daya yang memakai parit dan jembatan angkat rumah itu.
claims.quote: In Jack the Giant Killer, Thunderdell first appeared where he crashed a banquet that was prepared for Jack. During this time, he chanted "fee fau fum." Jack defeats and beheads the two-headed giant with a trick involving the house's moat and drawbridge.

claims.statement: According to one version of the story from 1800, Thunderdell (here called "Thunderful") hails from the North Pole; he attacks Jack's banquet to avenge the deaths of two giants he had earlier slain, but is defeated and his heads are sent to King Arthur's court.
claims.statement_id: Menurut satu versi cerita dari tahun 1800, Thunderdell (di sana disebut "Thunderful") berasal dari Kutub Utara; ia menyerang perjamuan Jack untuk membalas kematian dua raksasa yang pernah dibunuhnya, tetapi dikalahkan dan kepalanya dikirim ke istana Raja Arthur.
claims.quote: According to one version of the story from 1800, Thunderdell (here identified as "Thunderful") hails from the North Pole. He attacks Jack's banquet in order to avenge the deaths of two giants he had earlier slain, but is himself defeated and his heads sent to the court of King Arthur.

claims.statement: Film Jack and the Beanstalk: The Real Story, played by Bill Barretta.
claims.statement_id: Film Jack and the Beanstalk: The Real Story, diperankan Bill Barretta.
claims.quote: The Thunderdell name is used for a giant in Jack and the Beanstalk: The Real Story who was portrayed by Bill Barretta.

claims.statement: Thunderdell is Monster in My Pocket #98; es article: Thunderdel, Thunderel, Thunderbore.
claims.statement_id: Thunderdell adalah Monster in My Pocket #98; artikel es: Thunderdel, Thunderel, Thunderbore.
claims.quote: Thunderdell es el Monster in My Pocket #98.

claims.statement: In the tale, Thunderdell, a giant with two heads, having heard of the death of his kinsmen, came from the northern dales to be revenged on Jack.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita ini, Thunderdell, raksasa berkepala dua, mendengar kematian sanak-saudaranya dan datang dari lembah-lembah utara (northern dales) untuk membalas dendam kepada Jack.
claims.quote: that one Thunderdell, a giant with two heads, having heard of the death of his kinsmen, had come from the northern dales to be revenged on Jack

claims.statement: Thunderdell could not see Jack, but smelt his approach and cried out "Fee, fi, fo, fum! I smell the blood of an Englishman!".
claims.statement_id: Thunderdell tidak dapat melihat Jack, tetapi mencium kedatangannya dan berseru "Fee, fi, fo, fum! I smell the blood of an Englishman!".
claims.quote: one Thunderdell, a giant with two heads ... Although the giant could not see Jack, he smelt his approach, and cried out in these words: ... Fee, fi, fo, fum! I smell the blood of an Englishman!

claims.statement: The two-headed giant accuses Jack of killing his kinsmen and threatens to tear him with his teeth, suck his blood, and grind his bones to powder.
claims.statement_id: Si raksasa berkepala dua menuduh Jack membunuh sanak-saudaranya dan mengancam akan mencabik Jack dengan giginya, mengisap darahnya, dan menggiling tulangnya menjadi bubuk.
claims.quote: Art thou that villain who killed my kinsmen? Then I will tear thee with my teeth, suck thy blood, and grind thy bones to powder.

claims.statement: As the giant chased Jack over the drawbridge, his great weight broke the bridge and he tumbled headlong into the water.
claims.statement_id: Ketika si raksasa mengejar Jack di jembatan, beratnya yang besar mematahkan jembatan itu dan ia jatuh tersungkur ke air.
claims.quote: Then, coming to the middle of the bridge, the giant's great weight broke it down, and he tumbled headlong into the water, where he rolled and wallowed like a whale.

claims.statement: Jack cast a cart-rope over the giant's two heads, drew him ashore with a team of horses, then cut off both heads and sent them to King Arthur.
claims.statement_id: Jack menjerat kedua kepala si raksasa dengan tali gerobak, menariknya ke tepi dengan sekelompok kuda, lalu memenggal kedua kepalanya dan mengirimkannya kepada Raja Arthur.
claims.quote: Jack at length got a cart-rope and cast it over the two heads of the giant, and drew him ashore by a team of horses, and then cut off both his heads with his sword of sharpness, and sent them to King Arthur.

claims.statement: Aobh, a female figure of Irish Celtic mythology.
claims.statement_id: Aobh, tokoh perempuan mitologi Kelt Irlandia (Irlands).
claims.quote: Aobh ist eine weibliche Sagengestalt aus der keltischen Mythologie Irlands.

claims.statement: Daughter of Bodb Dearg, wife of Lir, king of the Túatha Dé Danann; bore twins twice (Fionnuala, Aed, Fiachra, Conn), died in childbirth; the Children of Lir.
claims.statement_id: Putri Bodb Dearg, istri Lir, raja Túatha Dé Danann; dua kali melahirkan kembar (Fionnuala, Aed, Fiachra, Conn), meninggal saat melahirkan; Anak-anak (Children of) Lir.
claims.quote: Sie ist die Tochter Bodb Deargs und die Gattin Lirs, des Königs der Túatha Dé Danann. Nachdem sie ihm zweimal Zwillinge geboren hat, stirbt sie im Kindbett.

claims.statement: Her children were to be killed at the will of her sister Aoife, Lir's second wife; a servant turned them into swans.
claims.statement_id: Anak-anaknya hendak dibunuh atas kehendak saudarinya Aoife, istri kedua Lir; pelayan mengubah mereka menjadi angsa.
claims.quote: Ihre Kinder, Fionnuala, Aed, Fiachra und Conn, sollen nach dem Willen ihrer Schwester Aoife, der zweiten Gemahlin Lirs, getötet werden, stattdessen verwandelt sie eine mitleidige Dienerin in Schwäne.

claims.statement: Áeb (Aobh, Aebh), a figure of Irish mythology.
claims.statement_id: Áeb (Aobh, Aebh), tokoh mitologi Irlandia.
claims.quote: Áeb, též Aobh či Aebh, je postava z irské mytologie.

claims.statement: Another version: a remorseful Aoife transformed them herself; the tale Oidheadh Chlainne Lir.
claims.statement_id: Versi lain: Aoife yang menyesal mengubah anak-anak itu sendiri; kisah Oidheadh Chlainne Lir.
claims.quote: Nach einer anderen Version soll Aoife, von Reue gepackt, die Kinder selbst verwandelt haben. Diese Erzählung ist als Oidheadh Chlainne Lir („Die Geschichte der Kinder Lirs“) überliefert.

claims.statement: Another version: she marries Manannan mac Lir, Lir's son.
claims.statement_id: Versi lain: menikah dengan Manannan mac Lir, putra Lir.
claims.quote: In einer anderen Version heiratet sie Manannan mac Lir, den Sohn Lirs.

claims.statement: Áeb, the eldest chosen, bore Finnguala and Áed, then Fiachra and Conn, and died in childbirth.
claims.statement_id: Áeb, putri tertua yang dipilih, melahirkan Finnguala dan Áed, lalu Fiachra dan Conn, dan meninggal saat melahirkan.
claims.quote: Vybrána je ta nejstarší, jménem Áeb, a ta Lirovi porodí jedny dvojčata, dceru Finngualu a syna Áeda, a poté další dvojčata Fiachru a Conna, při jejich porodu však zemře.

claims.statement: Per the Oidheadh Chloinne Lir, recorded in the 15th century, Bodb Derg of Connacht was chosen king of the Tuatha Dé Danann.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Oidheadh Chloinne Lir yang dicatat abad ke-15, Bodb Derg dari Connacht dipilih menjadi raja Tuatha Dé Danann.
claims.quote: Podle vyprávění Oidheadh Chloinne Lir „Tragického příběhu o dětech Lirových“ zaznamenaného v 15. století byl po bitvě u Tailtiu zvolen králem Tuatha Dé Danann Bodb Derg z Connachtu

claims.statement: Arausio, a local Celtic god at Arausio in southern Gaul, now Orange in southern France.
claims.statement_id: Arausio, dewa Kelt setempat di Arausio, Galia (Gaul) selatan, kini Orange, Prancis (France) selatan.
claims.quote: Arausio was a local Celtic god who was venerated in the settlement of Arausio in southern Gaul, now Orange in southern France.

claims.statement: A local Celtic water god; ancient inscriptions show the town Arausio (Orange) in southern Gaul was named after him.
claims.statement_id: Dewa air Kelt setempat; menurut prasasti kuno kota Arausio (Orange) di Galia selatan dinamai menurut dia.
claims.quote: Arausio byl lokální keltský vodní bůh. Jak dokládají starověké nápisy bylo po něm pojmenováno město Arausio (Orange) v jižní Galii.

claims.statement: zh article: a Celtic river deity, honoured in southern Gaul under Roman rule, known from inscriptions on finds.
claims.statement_id: Artikel zh: dewa sungai Kelt, dipuja di Galia selatan masa Romawi, dikenal dari prasasti temuan arkeologis.
claims.quote: 凯尔特职司河流的神祇之一。盛行于罗马统治时期的高卢南部地区，其事迹反映于相关出土的文物之铭文。

claims.statement: Per the Wikipedia article on Orange, a Celtic settlement called Aurasio existed in the same place, named after a local sacred spring.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Wikipedia tentang Orange, permukiman Celtic bernama Aurasio pernah ada di tempat yang sama dan dinamai menurut sebuah mata air suci setempat.
claims.quote: A Celtic settlement called Aurasio existed in the same place, named after a local sacred spring.

claims.statement: Per the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur tourism site, a sacred spring gave its name, Arausio, to the site, which later became known as Orange.
claims.statement_id: Menurut situs pariwisata wilayah Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, sebuah mata air suci memberi nama Arausio kepada lokasi itu, yang kemudian dikenal sebagai Orange.
claims.quote: A sacred spring gave its name, Arausio, to the site, which later became known as Orange.

claims.statement: Per the Wikipedia article on Orange, the place-name derives from Proto-Celtic *far-aws(y)o-, literally "in front of the ear", which became Gaulish ar-aus(i)o- ("temple, cheek").
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Wikipedia tentang Orange, nama tempat itu berasal dari bentuk Proto-Celtic *far-aws(y)o- yang secara harfiah berarti "di depan telinga", lalu menjadi ar-aus(i)o- dalam bahasa Galia ("kuil, pipi").
claims.quote: The name itself derived from an earlier Proto-Celtic *far-aws(y)o-, which literally means 'in front of the ear' ... This became the Gaulish ar-aus(i)o- ('temple, cheek').

claims.statement: Per the Czech Wikipedia article, in a later period the name of the town Arausio fell out of use and Orange began to be used.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Wikipedia bahasa Ceko, pada masa kemudian nama kota Arausio hilang dari pemakaian dan nama Orange mulai dipakai.
claims.quote: V pozdější době jméno města Arausio zaniklo a začalo se používat Orange.

claims.statement: The asrai, an aquatic fairy of English folklore and literature, female, lake-dwelling, like the mermaid and nixie; possibly invented by Scottish poet Robert Williams Buchanan.
claims.statement_id: Asrai, peri air folklor dan sastra Inggris (English), perempuan, tinggal di danau, mirip putri duyung dan nixie; mungkin ciptaan penyair Skotlandia (Scottish) Robert Williams Buchanan.
claims.quote: The asrai is a type of aquatic fairy in English folklore and literature. They are usually depicted as female, live in lakes and are similar to the mermaid and nixie. Rather than originating from folklore, the asrai may have been invented by the Scottish poet Robert Williams Buchanan.

claims.statement: Spellings Asrey or ashray; the poem The Asrai by Robert Williams Buchanan, April 1872.
claims.statement_id: Ejaan Asrey atau ashray; puisi The Asrai karya Robert Williams Buchanan, April 1872.
claims.quote: "Asrey" or "ashray" sometimes appear as spelling variants. It is unclear whether the asrai was ever part of folk belief. Their oldest known appearance in print was the poem "The Asrai" by Robert Williams Buchanan, first published in April 1872

claims.statement: In Buchanan's poetry: pale, gentle, older than humanity, fearing light, living under a lake.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi Buchanan: pucat, lembut, lebih tua dari manusia, takut cahaya, hidup di bawah danau.
claims.quote: In Buchanan's poetry, the asrai are pale, gentle beings, older than humanity, who fear light and live beneath a lake.

claims.statement: Ruth Tongue, British storyteller of questioned reliability.
claims.statement_id: Ruth Tongue, pencerita Inggris (British), keandalannya diragukan.
claims.quote: The asrai gained renewed attention through the works of British storyteller Ruth Tongue, whose reliability as a folklorist has been questioned.

claims.statement: The asrai melted into a puddle when exposed too long to the sun.
claims.statement_id: Asrai mencair menjadi genangan air bila terlalu lama terkena matahari.
claims.quote: By the time the fisherman reached the shore, the asrai had melted away leaving nothing but a puddle of water in the boat, for the asrai perish if directly exposed too long to the sun.

claims.statement: Ruth Tongue: Cheshire, Shropshire, the Welsh Border; shy, beautiful, webbed feet, green hair; surfaces once a century to bathe in moonlight; a fisherman burned by its touch.
claims.statement_id: Ruth Tongue: Cheshire, Shropshire, perbatasan Wales (Welsh Border); pemalu, cantik, kaki berselaput, rambut hijau; muncul sekali seabad mandi cahaya bulan; nelayan terbakar sentuhannya.
claims.quote: Ruth Tongue attributed stories of the asrai to Cheshire, Shropshire, and the Welsh Border. In her collected work, the asrai are timid and shy, very beautiful, and have webbed feet and green hair.

claims.statement: sv article: an asrai touched by sunlight or caught dies and collapses into a puddle.
claims.statement_id: Artikel sv: asrai yang tersentuh sinar matahari atau ditangkap akan mati menjadi genangan air.
claims.quote: Om en Asrai nuddar solljuset eller fångas så dör den, och faller ihop i en vattenpöl.

claims.statement: Baloma is the spirit of the dead in Trobriand society (Trobriand Islands, Papua New Guinea), studied by Bronislaw Malinowski in the early 20th century, who published an article on it in 1916.
claims.statement_id: Baloma adalah roh orang mati dalam masyarakat Trobriand (Kepulauan Trobriand, Papua Nugini); Bronislaw Malinowski mempelajarinya pada awal abad ke-20 dan menerbitkan artikel tentangnya pada 1916.
claims.quote: Baloma is the spirit of the dead in Trobriand society, as studied by Bronislaw Malinowski in the early 20th century, who published an article on it in 1916

claims.statement: Replaces the role of male sperm (fathers) in conception; maintains matrilineal descent.
claims.statement_id: Menggantikan peran sperma laki-laki (ayah) dalam pembuahan; menopang keturunan matrilineal.
claims.quote: It plays a key role in conception ideologies and explains and maintains the matrilineal descent system by substituting the role of male sperm ("fathers") with that of a spirit.

claims.statement: Spirit of a deceased lineage member impregnating women bathing in the sea.
claims.statement_id: Roh anggota garis keturunan yang membuahi perempuan saat mandi di laut.
claims.quote: The baloma is that spirit of a deceased lineage member which impregnates the women while bathing in the sea, perpetuating the matrilineage intragenerationally.

claims.statement: Intercourse only opens the path for the baloma into the womb.
claims.statement_id: Hubungan seksual hanya membuka jalan bagi baloma ke rahim.
claims.quote: The role of sexual intercourse is only indirectly related to conception within Trobriand mentality and seen as a way of opening the path for the baloma to enter the woman's womb.

claims.statement: pl article: pregnancy through sea bathing; basis of Trobriand matrilineal inheritance.
claims.statement_id: Artikel pl: hamil lewat mandi di laut; dasar pewarisan matrilineal orang Trobriand.
claims.quote: Można zajść w ciążę, kąpiąc się w morzu. Stosunek seksualny ma rolę drugorzędną, stanowi zaledwie sposób otwarcia drogi dla baloma. Wierzenia te stanowią podstawę matrylinearnego systemu dziedziczenia wśród Trobriandczyków.

claims.statement: Per Malinowski, the spirits of the dead of the Trobrianders migrate immediately after death to the island of Tuma and return once a year to visit their villages and take part in the annual milamala feast, where they receive offerings.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Malinowski, roh orang mati orang Trobriand segera setelah kematian pindah ke pulau Tuma dan setahun sekali mengunjungi desa mereka serta ikut pesta tahunan milamala dan menerima persembahan.
claims.quote: some of the magico-religious ideas of the Trobrianders ... The spirits migrate immediately after death to the island of Tuma, lying in the North-West of Boyowa ... They return to visit their own villages once a year, and take part in the big annual feast, milamala, where they receive offerings.

claims.statement: Malinowski notes that in their belief in the spirits of the dead, the Trobrianders are almost completely devoid of any fear of ghosts.
claims.statement_id: Malinowski mencatat bahwa dalam kepercayaan mereka tentang roh orang mati, orang Trobriand hampir sepenuhnya tidak takut pada hantu.
claims.quote: A few more words must be said about some of the magico-religious ideas of the Trobrianders. The main thing that struck me in connection with their belief in the spirits of the dead, was that they are almost completely devoid of any fear of ghosts

claims.statement: Per Malinowski, the ula'ula, a special type of magical payment, is at the same time an offering to the baloma (spirits).
claims.statement_id: Menurut Malinowski, ula'ula, sejenis pembayaran sihir khusus, sekaligus merupakan persembahan kepada baloma (roh).
claims.quote: A special type of magical payment, the ula'ula, is at the same time an offering to the baloma (spirits).

claims.statement: Per Malinowski, in some cases the baloma will appear in dreams and advise the magician what to do.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Malinowski, dalam beberapa kasus baloma muncul dalam mimpi dan menasihati pesihir tentang apa yang harus dilakukan.
claims.quote: In some cases the baloma will appear in dreams and advise the magician what to do.

claims.statement: Malinowski interprets that the baloma would go no further than to reproach people for breaking the old rules, and that these natives have no definite ideas about actual punishment meted out by offended spirits.
claims.statement_id: Malinowski menafsirkan bahwa baloma paling jauh hanya menegur orang yang melanggar aturan lama, dan tidak ada gagasan pasti di kalangan penduduk tentang hukuman nyata dari roh yang tersinggung.
claims.quote: The baloma would go no further than to reproach them for breaking the old rules, and there are no definite ideas among these natives about actual punishment being meted out by offended spirits.

claims.statement: Per Malinowski, the baloma (spirits) of the ancestors are asked to sit on the canoe slips and chew betel.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Malinowski, baloma (roh) para leluhur diminta duduk di landasan kano (canoe slips) dan mengunyah sirih.
claims.quote: Then the baloma (spirits) of these ancestors are asked to sit on the canoe slips and to chew betel

claims.statement: Bisterne Dragon, a New Forest legend, England; Bisterne, Burley, Lyndhurst.
claims.statement_id: Naga Bisterne (Bisterne Dragon), legenda New Forest, Inggris (England); Bisterne, Burley, Lyndhurst.
claims.quote: The Bisterne Dragon is a legend from the New Forest in England. The story takes place primarily in Bisterne, but also features Burley and Lyndhurst, and is one of the area's most famous pieces of folklore.

claims.statement: Den at Burley Beacon, 3 miles east of Bisterne; flew each morning to be given milk.
claims.statement_id: Sarang di Burley Beacon, 3 mil timur Bisterne; terbang tiap pagi untuk diberi susu.
claims.quote: The local tradition is that a dragon had his den at Burley Beacon, about 3 miles (4.8 km) east of Bisterne, at Burley. There are several versions of the tale, one being that the creature "flew" every morning to Bisterne, where it would be supplied with milk.

claims.statement: A knight named Berkeley lay in wait with two dogs.
claims.statement_id: Ksatria bernama Berkeley menunggu bersama dua anjing.
claims.quote: In order to kill the dragon, a valiant knight (usually named Berkeley) built a hide, and with two dogs lay in wait.

claims.statement: The dragon died outside Lyndhurst, its corpse becoming the hill Boltons Bench; armour covered with glass.
claims.statement_id: Naga mati di luar Lyndhurst, tubuhnya menjadi bukit Boltons Bench; zirah berlapis kaca.
claims.quote: with the dragon finally dying outside the village of Lyndhurst, his corpse turning into a hill (now known as Boltons Bench)

claims.statement: A pedigree roll before 1618 at Berkeley Castle names Sir Maurice Berkeley, 15th-century lord of Bisterne; dragon-and-beacon crest.
claims.statement_id: Silsilah sebelum 1618 di Berkeley Castle menyebut Sir Maurice Berkeley, tuan tanah Bisterne abad ke-15; lambang naga di depan suar.
claims.quote: The documentary version of this tradition is contained in the margin of a pedigree roll written prior to 1618, and preserved at Berkeley Castle. It actually names the dragon-slayer as Sir Maurice Berkeley, lord of the manor of Bisterne in the 15th century

claims.statement: The fight site is called Dragon Fields.
claims.statement_id: Lokasi pertarungan disebut Dragon Fields.
claims.quote: The alleged scene of the fight in Bisterne is still called "Dragon Fields"

claims.statement: ja article (Hampshire dragon): the dragon demanded the flesh of livestock and people.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ja (Hampshire dragon): naga menuntut daging ternak dan manusia.
claims.quote: バーリー山に棲む竜は、毎日のようにビスターン村に現れては手桶1杯分の牛乳を村人たちに要求していた。やがて竜は家畜の肉や人の肉まで求めるようになった。

claims.statement: Blue Ben, a legendary dragon of Kilve, western Somerset, England; an Ichthyosaur skull.
claims.statement_id: Blue Ben, naga legenda dari Kilve, Somerset barat, Inggris (England); tengkorak Ichthyosaur.
claims.quote: Blue Ben is a legendary dragon from Kilve in western Somerset, England. The skull of a fossilized Ichthyosaur on display in a local museum is sometimes pointed out as belonging to him.

claims.statement: Dwells in shale caves of the Somerset coast, bathing after breathing fire.
claims.statement_id: Tinggal di gua serpih pesisir Somerset, berendam setelah menyemburkan api.
claims.quote: Blue Ben typically dwells in the shale caves along the Somerset coast, regularly bathing in the nearby waters to cool himself after breathing fire.

claims.statement: The Devil rode him through the fires of Hell; limestone causeway.
claims.statement_id: Iblis (Devil) menungganginya melewati api neraka (Hell); jalan batu kapur.
claims.quote: The Devil, who had watched Blue Ben for some time, decided to capture him for use as a mount. The Devil rode the dragon mercilessly through the fires of Hell until the dragon escaped.

claims.statement: Blue Ben got stuck and was consumed by the mud.
claims.statement_id: Blue Ben terjebak dan ditelan lumpur.
claims.quote: Hurrying to get back to the security of his lair, Blue Ben made the mistake of tramping through the mud flats. He got stuck in the mud, which consumed him.

claims.statement: Early 19th-century Blue Lias quarrying uncovered an Ichthyosaur skull; Wells and Mendip Museum, Wells; Museum of Somerset, Taunton.
claims.statement_id: Penambangan Blue Lias awal abad ke-19 menemukan tengkorak Ichthyosaur; Wells and Mendip Museum, Wells; Museum of Somerset, Taunton.
claims.quote: In the early 19th century, the Blue Lias shale formation outside of Kilve was quarried, during which process the fossilized skull of an Ichthyosaur was uncovered, that was said to be the remains of Blue Ben.

claims.statement: fa article: a legendary dragon from Kilve, a village in west Somerset, England.
claims.statement_id: Artikel fa: naga legenda dari Kilve, desa di Somerset barat, Inggris.
claims.quote: یک اژدهای افسانه‌ای از کیلوِه (دهکده‌ای در سامرست غربی، انگلستان) است.

claims.statement: Bogle (boggle, bogill), a Northumbrian, Cumbrian and Scots term for a ghost; Shellycoats, Barghests, Brags, the Hedley Kow, giants; similar to the boggart. England and Scotland.
claims.statement_id: Bogle (boggle, bogill), istilah Northumbria (Northumbrian), Cumbria (Cumbrian) dan Skotlandia (Scots) untuk hantu; Shellycoat, Barghest, Brag, Hedley Kow, raksasa; mirip boggart. Inggris (England) dan Skotlandia (Scotland).
claims.quote: is a Northumbrian, Cumbrian and Scots term for a ghost or folkloric being, used for a variety of related folkloric creatures including Shellycoats, Barghests, Brags, the Hedley Kow and even giants

claims.statement: Live to perplex mankind.
claims.statement_id: Hidup untuk membingungkan manusia.
claims.quote: They are reputed to live for the simple purpose of perplexing mankind, rather than seriously harming or serving them.

claims.statement: Tatty Bogle hid in potato fields, attacking people or blighting crops; a scarecrow.
claims.statement_id: Tatty Bogle bersembunyi di ladang kentang, menyerang manusia atau merusak tanaman; orang-orangan sawah.
claims.quote: There is a popular story of a bogle known as Tatty Bogle, who would hide himself in potato fields (hence his name) and either attack unwary humans or cause blight within the patch. This bogle was depicted as a scarecrow

claims.statement: From Middle English Bugge; also the source of bogey.
claims.statement_id: Dari kata Inggris Pertengahan (Middle-English) Bugge; asal kata bogey.
claims.quote: The name is derived from the Middle-English Bugge (from which the term bogey is also derived)

claims.statement: Gavin Douglas, quoted by Robert Burns in Tam O' Shanter.
claims.statement_id: Gavin Douglas, dikutip Robert Burns dalam Tam O' Shanter.
claims.quote: One of the most famous usages of the term was by Gavin Douglas, who was in turn quoted by Robert Burns at the beginning of Tam O' Shanter: Of Brownyis and of Bogillis full is this Buke.

claims.statement: Bòcan (Scottish Gaelic): a demon, evil fairy or ghost.
claims.statement_id: Bòcan (Gaelik Skotlandia, Scottish Gaelic): setan, peri jahat atau hantu.
claims.quote: Tha bòcan na dheamhain. 'S e Sìthiche olc neo taibhse.

claims.statement: A lake monster in Windermere, Cumbria, England, like that of Loch Ness; photographed 2011; nicknamed Bownessie.
claims.statement_id: Monster danau di Windermere, Cumbria, Inggris (England), mirip Loch Ness; difoto 2011; dijuluki Bownessie.
claims.quote: Some people believe that there may be a lake monster, similar to the one alleged to live in Loch Ness, and in 2011 anomalous photos were taken of the supposed creature; it has been affectionately nicknamed "Bownessie".

claims.statement: Windermere is a ribbon lake in Cumbria, England, within the Lake District, and the largest lake in England by length, area, and volume.
claims.statement_id: Windermere adalah danau pita di Cumbria, Inggris, di Lake District, dan danau terbesar di Inggris menurut panjang, luas, dan volume.
claims.quote: Windermere (historically Winder Mere) is a ribbon lake in Cumbria, England. It is within the Lake District and is the largest lake in England by length, area, and volume

claims.statement: Per the French Wikipedia article, Bownessie was named in tribute to its famous "cousin" "living" in a freshwater lake in Scotland, the Loch Ness monster nicknamed Nessie; it too is described as resembling a sea serpent or a plesiosaur.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Wikipedia bahasa Prancis, Bownessie dinamai sebagai penghormatan bagi "sepupunya" yang "hidup" di danau air tawar Skotlandia, monster Loch Ness yang dijuluki Nessie; ia juga digambarkan mirip ular laut atau plesiosaurus.
claims.quote: Elle a été baptisée « Bownessie », en hommage a son célèbre « cousin » « vivant » dans un lac d'eau douce d'Écosse, le Monstre du Loch Ness, surnommé Nessie (parfois orthographié Nessy). Bownessie est, elle aussi, décrite comme ressemblant à un serpent de mer ou à un plésiosaure.

claims.statement: Per the French Wikipedia article, after fresh claims by tourists in February 2011, Dr Ian Winfield of the Lancaster University centre for ecology and hydrology said no fish as large as the descriptions given could live in Lake Windermere, and that the lake is surveyed every month and nothing of the kind has ever been found.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Wikipedia bahasa Prancis, setelah klaim baru wisatawan pada Februari 2011, Dr Ian Winfield dari pusat ekologi dan hidrologi Universitas Lancaster menyatakan tidak ada ikan sebesar gambaran yang diberikan yang bisa hidup di danau Windermere, dan bahwa danau itu diperiksa setiap bulan tanpa pernah ditemukan hal semacam itu.
claims.quote: À la suite de nouvelles affirmations de touristes en février 2011, le docteur Ian Winfield, du centre d'écologie et d'hydrologie de l’Université de Lancaster a déclaré : « Aucun poisson aussi grand que les descriptions que l’on nous a données ne pourrait vivre dans le lac Windermere », et il a précisé que « le lieu est sondé tous les mois et que rien de tel n'a jamais été trouvé ».

claims.statement: Per the French Wikipedia article citing The Telegraph, the new photograph matched the description given by Steve Burnip in 2006; to that date nine people had claimed to see "Bownessie".
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Wikipedia bahasa Prancis yang merujuk The Telegraph, foto baru itu cocok dengan gambaran yang diberikan Steve Burnip pada 2006; hingga saat itu sembilan orang mengaku pernah melihat "Bownessie".
claims.quote: Selon The Telegraph, cette nouvelle photo faite, du « monstre » correspond à la description qu’en avait fait Steve Burnip en 2006. À ce jour, neuf personnes ont donc affirmé avoir aperçu « Bownessie ».

claims.statement: Per NBC News, Tom Pickles and Sara Harrington, work colleagues kayaking at the lake as a team-building exercise, photographed the possible sea creature with a mobile phone.
claims.statement_id: Menurut NBC News, Tom Pickles dan Sara Harrington, rekan kerja yang berkayak di danau sebagai latihan membangun tim, memotret kemungkinan makhluk laut itu dengan telepon seluler.
claims.quote: Tom Pickles and Sara Harrington, work colleagues who were kayaking at the lake as part of a team-building exercise, snapped this photo of the possible sea creature with a mobile phone.

claims.statement: Per NBC News, the photo appears to show a multi-humped black object moving through the water from left to right; Pickles described it as "a giant dark brown snake with humps measuring three car lengths" with a seal-like skin texture but a "completely abnormal" shape.
claims.statement_id: Menurut NBC News, foto itu tampak menunjukkan benda hitam berpunuk banyak bergerak di air dari kiri ke kanan; Pickles menggambarkannya sebagai "ular cokelat tua raksasa dengan punuk sepanjang tiga mobil" bertekstur kulit seperti anjing laut tetapi berbentuk "sangat tidak normal".
claims.quote: It appears to show a multi-humped black object moving through the water from left to right. Pickles described the object as "a giant dark brown snake with humps measuring three car lengths," and said it had seal-like skin texture but with a "completely abnormal" shape.

claims.statement: Per NBC News, skeptics say the so-called "Bownessie" of England's Lake Windermere could be a hoax.
claims.statement_id: Menurut NBC News, para skeptis mengatakan "Bownessie" yang konon ada di Danau Windermere, Inggris, bisa jadi tipuan.
claims.quote: but skeptics say the so-called "Bownessie" of England's Lake Windermere could be a hoax.

claims.statement: Per NBC News, the name "Bownessie" is named for Bowness, the local town in England.
claims.statement_id: Menurut NBC News, nama "Bownessie" diambil dari Bowness, kota setempat di Inggris.
claims.quote: While the case of the "Bownessie" (named for Bowness, the local town in England) may not hold up to scrutiny

claims.statement: Bugbear, a type of hobgoblin, like the boogeyman (bugaboo, babau, cucuy); frightens disobedient children.
claims.statement_id: Bugbear, sejenis hobgoblin, mirip boogeyman (bugaboo, babau, cucuy); menakuti anak tidak patuh.
