claims.quote: A bugbear is a legendary creature or type of hobgoblin comparable to the boogeyman (or bugaboo or babau or cucuy), and other creatures of folklore, all of which were historically used in some cultures to frighten disobedient children.

claims.statement: In medieval England: a creepy bear in the woods; name from Middle English bugge, Old Welsh bwg, Old Scots bogill.
claims.statement_id: Di Inggris (England) abad pertengahan: beruang seram di hutan; nama dari Inggris Pertengahan bugge, Welsh Kuno bwg, Skots Kuno bogill.
claims.quote: In medieval England, the bugbear was depicted as a creepy bear that lurked in the woods to scare children.

claims.statement: The Buggbears, adapted from Antonio Francesco Grazzini's La Spiritata (1561).
claims.statement_id: The Buggbears, saduran La Spiritata karya Antonio Francesco Grazzini (1561).
claims.quote: It was described in this manner in The Buggbears, an adaptation, with additions, from Antonio Francesco Grazzini’s La Spiritata (‘The Possessed [Woman]’, 1561).

claims.statement: Large hairy goblinoid monsters in fantasy role-playing games.
claims.statement_id: Monster goblinoid besar berbulu dalam permainan peran fantasi.
claims.quote: They also appear as monsters, described as large, hairy goblinoids, in the canon of popular fantasy role-playing games.

claims.statement: Also called Bugaboo, Bogglebo, Bugs.
claims.statement_id: Juga disebut Bugaboo, Bogglebo, Bugs.
claims.quote: バガブー (Bugaboo)、ボグルボー (Bogglebo) 、またはバグス (Bugs)とも。

claims.statement: ja article: mothers warn naughty children that the bugbear (バグベア) will eat them.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ja: para ibu menakuti anak nakal bahwa mereka akan dimakan bugbear (バグベア).
claims.quote: 母親達は言う事を聞かない子に「あんたみたいな悪い子はバグベアに食べられてしまうよ」と脅かすという。

claims.statement: Caoineag, female spirit of Scottish folklore, Highland banshee, the weeper; invisible; laments at night at waterfall, stream, loch, glen, mountainside; unapproachable unlike the bean nighe.
claims.statement_id: Caoineag, roh perempuan folklor Skotlandia (Scottish), banshee Dataran Tinggi (Highland), si peratap; tak terlihat; meratap malam di air terjun, sungai, loch (Loch), lembah, lereng; tak dapat didekati seperti bean nighe.
claims.quote: is a female spirit in Scottish folklore and a type of Highland banshee, her name meaning "weeper". She is normally invisible and foretells death in her clan by lamenting in the night at a waterfall, stream or Loch, or in a glen or on a mountainside.

claims.statement: Other names: caointeag, caoineachag, caointeachag, caoidheag.
claims.statement_id: Nama lain: caointeag, caoineachag, caointeachag, caoidheag.
claims.quote: Other local names for her include caointeag, caoineachag, caointeachag, and caoidheag.

claims.statement: Alexander Carmichael (Carmina Gadelica): foretells deaths in battle.
claims.statement_id: Alexander Carmichael (Carmina Gadelica): meramalkan kematian dalam perang.
claims.quote: The Scottish folklorist Alexander Carmichael in Carmina Gadelica states that she foretells the death of those slain in battle

claims.statement: Before the Massacre of Glencoe the caoineag of Clan MacDonald wailed; those who left escaped.
claims.statement_id: Sebelum Pembantaian (Massacre of) Glencoe, caoineag Klan (Clan) MacDonald meratap; yang pergi selamat.
claims.quote: Before the Massacre of Glencoe, the caoineag of Clan MacDonald was heard to wail night after night. Those whose fears were roused by her keening left the glen and escaped the fate of those who remained behind.

claims.statement: The caointeach of Islay: green shawl, laments at the sick person's door; sometimes conflated with the bean nighe.
claims.statement_id: Caointeach di Islay: berselendang hijau, meratap di pintu orang sakit; kadang disamakan dengan bean nighe.
claims.quote: The caointeach is another version of this death spirit attached to various clans in Islay. When a death from illness was about to occur, she would appear outside the sick person's house wearing a green shawl and begin lamenting at the door.

claims.statement: gd article: asked Cò tha siud (who is there), she answers: Caoineag bheag a' bhròin, little Caoineag of the sorrow.
claims.statement_id: Artikel gd: ditanya Cò tha siud (siapa itu), ia menjawab: Caoineag bheag a' bhròin, Caoineag kecil yang berduka.
claims.quote: Do neach a dh' iarr "Cò tha siud?", dh'fhreagradh i: "Cò a th' ann ach Caoineag bheag a' bhròin!"

claims.statement: Coblyn (koblyn, coblynau, coblynod), gnome-like, haunts mines of Wales and Welsh settlements in America.
claims.statement_id: Coblyn (koblyn, coblynau, coblynod), mirip gnome, menghuni tambang di Wales dan permukiman Welsh di Amerika (America).
claims.quote: is a mythical gnome-like creature that is said to haunt the mines and quarries of Wales and areas of Welsh settlements in America.

claims.statement: Wirt Sikes (British Goblins): friendly fairies, short, very ugly, in miners' clothing.
claims.statement_id: Wirt Sikes (British Goblins): peri ramah, pendek, sangat jelek, berpakaian penambang.
claims.quote: In British Goblins, Wirt Sikes describes coblynau as friendly fairies, short (between half a yard tall and just shorter than humans), very ugly, and often dressed in miner's clothing

claims.statement: Like Cornish Knockers, lead to ore veins; throw rocks; good luck.
claims.statement_id: Seperti Knocker Cornwall (Cornish), menuntun ke urat bijih; lempar batu; pembawa untung.
claims.quote: Like the Knockers of Cornish folklore, they often help miners to the richest veins of ore or other treasures by their peculiar knocking sound. They may throw rocks at miners if disrespected, but the rocks are typically harmless. Miners generally consider coblynau to be good luck.

claims.statement: Fifteen or sixteen coblynau in red Morris dancing in a Bodfari field.
claims.statement_id: Lima belas atau enam belas coblynau berpakaian merah menari Morris di ladang Bodfari.
claims.quote: One account tells of a group of children seeing a group of fifteen or sixteen coblynau, dressed in all red and wearing yellow-spotted red handkerchiefs around their heads, Morris dancing in a Bodfari field.

claims.statement: Coblyn related to Goblin, Kobold, Gobelin; William Salesbury's 1547 dictionary.
claims.statement_id: Kata Coblyn berkerabat dengan Goblin (goblin), Kobold, Gobelin; kamus William Salesbury 1547. Kamus bahasa Welsh dan Inggris (English).
claims.quote: The word Coblyn is related to the English word Goblin, and may derive from a Germanic source akin to the German Kobold, via the French Gobelin. It appears in William Salesbury's 1547 Welsh-English dictionary as koblyn

claims.statement: nl article: related to the Cornish Knockers, Blue Cap, Kaolmenke, Wichtel; dancing at Bodfari.
claims.statement_id: Artikel nl: berkerabat dengan Knockers Cornwall, Blue Cap, Kaolmenke, Wichtel; menari di Bodfari.
claims.quote: De Coblynau is verwant met de Knockers uit Cornwall, het wezen heeft overeenkomsten met de Blue Cap en het Kaolmenke uit de Lage Landen en de Wichtel uit Zuid-Duitsland.

claims.statement: El Sombrerón, legend of Guatemala and bogeyman in Mexico; Tzipitio, Tzizimite; man in black, shining belt, large black hat, noisy boots.
claims.statement_id: El Sombrerón, legenda Guatemala dan sosok penakut di Meksiko (Mexico); Tzipitio, Tzizimite; lelaki berpakaian hitam, sabuk mengilap, topi hitam besar, bot berisik.
claims.quote: This character is also known with other names, like Tzipitio, the goblin, and sometimes Tzizimite, his main characteristics are always the same: a tall man with black dress, a thick and brilliant belt; he wears a black, large hat, and boots that make a lot of noise when he walks.

claims.statement: Braids horses' tails and manes, dogs' hair; courts long-haired girls.
claims.statement_id: Mengepang ekor dan surai kuda, bulu anjing; mendekati gadis berambut panjang.
claims.quote: He likes to ride horses and braid their tails and manes. When he cannot find horses, he braids the hair of dogs. He also likes to court young ladies who have long hair and big eyes.

claims.statement: Braids the girl's hair, serenades with a silver guitar, puts soil in her plate; she cannot eat or sleep.
claims.statement_id: Mengepang rambut gadis, serenade dengan gitar perak, menaruh tanah di piringnya; gadis tak bisa makan atau tidur.
claims.quote: When he likes one in particular, he follows her, braids her hair, and serenades to her with his silver guitar; but he also puts soil in her plate and she is not able to eat or sleep.

claims.statement: Appears at dusk with coal-laden mules; La Recolección; with La Llorona, Cadejo, Siguanaba among Guatemala's key legends.
claims.statement_id: Muncul senja dengan bagal pengangkut arang; La Recolección; bersama La Llorona, Cadejo, Siguanaba legenda penting Guatemala.
claims.quote: El Sombrerón appears at dusk, dragging along a group of mules carrying coal, with whom he travels around the city and its neighborhoods.

claims.statement: Miguel Ángel Asturias, Legends of Guatemala (1930); 1950 film; Susana's hair cut and taken to church.
claims.statement_id: Miguel Ángel Asturias, Legends of Guatemala (1930); film 1950; kisah Susana rambut dipotong dan dibawa ke gereja.
claims.quote: "Legend of El Sombrerón" is the title of one of the short stories in Guatemalan Nobel-prize winner Miguel Ángel Asturias' 1930 collection Legends of Guatemala. In 1950, El Sombrerón became the subject of an eponymous film, one of the first films shot in Guatemala.

claims.statement: es article: Tzitzimite, a dwarf with a huge hat who serenades women; braids hair at night.
claims.statement_id: Artikel es: Tzitzimite, kurcaci bertopi besar yang memberi serenade; mengepang rambut di malam hari.
claims.quote: El Sombrerón, también llamado Tzitzimite, es un personaje mitológico de una de las más conocidas  Leyendas de Guatemala, reflejado en libros y en el cine. Está representado como un enano que lleva consigo un enorme sombrero, dando serenatas a las mujeres que elige.

claims.statement: Eloko (pl. Biloko), a dwarf-like forest creature in a Mongo-Nkundo language; ancestral spirits.
claims.statement_id: Eloko (jamak Biloko), makhluk mirip kurcaci dalam bahasa Mongo-Nkundo, tinggal di hutan; roh leluhur.
claims.quote: Eloko (pl. Biloko) is a term in a Mongo-Nkundo language referring to a kind of dwarf-like creature that lives in the forests. They are believed to be the spirits of ancestors of the people living there.

claims.statement: Rainforest of central Zaïre (Congo, Africa); guard game and rare fruits; grudge against the living.
claims.statement_id: Hutan hujan Zaïre tengah (Kongo, Afrika); menjaga hewan buruan dan buah langka; dendam pada orang hidup.
claims.quote: Biloko live in the densest and darkest part of the rain forest in central Zaïre, jealously and ferociously guarding their treasures: the game and the rare fruits of the forest.

claims.statement: Live in hollow trees, dressed in leaves, grass-covered, wide mouths, long claws.
claims.statement_id: Tinggal di pohon berongga, berpakaian daun, berumput, bermulut lebar, bercakar panjang.
claims.quote: The Biloko live in hollow trees and are dressed only in leaves. They have no hair; only grass grows on their bodies; they have piercing eyes, snouts with mouths that can be opened wide enough to admit a human body

claims.statement: Little bells that enchant in Central Africa; amulets protect.
claims.statement_id: Lonceng kecil penyihir di Afrika Tengah (Central Africa); jimat melindungi.
claims.quote: They possess little bells, which, in Central Africa are believed to be able to cast a spell on passers-by. Possessing an amulet or a fetish can offer protection from this type of magic.

claims.statement: Tale cited by Bantu linguist Jan Knappert: the eloko refuses food, eats only human meat; the husband finds his wife's bones.
claims.statement_id: Kisah ahli bahasa Bantu Jan Knappert: eloko menolak makanan, hanya makan daging manusia; sang suami menemukan tulang istrinya.
claims.quote: She offered him banana mash with fried fish but he refused: "We eat only human meat. I have not eaten for a long time. Give me a piece of your arm."

claims.statement: An Eloko antagonist in Marlon James's Dark Star trilogy (Black Leopard, Red Wolf).
claims.statement_id: Eloko antagonis dalam trilogi Dark Star karya Marlon James (Black Leopard, Red Wolf).
claims.quote: An Eloko serves as a major antagonist in the Dark Star trilogy by Marlon James and appears in both books Black Leopard, Red Wolf and Moon Witch, Spider King.

claims.statement: ha article: Biloko live in hollow trees and wear only leaves.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ha: Biloko tinggal di pohon berongga dan hanya berpakaian daun.
claims.quote: Biloko suna zaune a cikin bishiyoyi masu rami kuma suna sanye da ganye kawai.

claims.statement: Failinis (Ṡalinnis, Shalinnis), a dog of the Irish Mythological Cycle, owned by Lugh Lámhfhada of the Tuatha Dé Danann; eric from the sons of Tuireann; whelp of the smith or king of Iruaith (Ioruath).
claims.statement_id: Failinis (Ṡalinnis, Shalinnis), anjing Siklus Mitologis (Mythological Cycle) Irlandia (Irish), milik Lugh Lámhfhada dari Tuatha Dé Danann; eric dari putra Tuireann; anak anjing pandai besi atau raja Iruaith (Ioruath).
claims.quote: is a dog in the Mythological Cycle of Irish literature, belonging to Lugh Lámhfhada of the Tuatha Dé Danann; it was one of the eric (reparation) items exacted from the sons of Tuireann. It was originally the hound-whelp of the smith or the king of Iruaith (Ioruath, Hiruaidhe, etc.).

claims.statement: Unnamed in the 12th-century Lebor Gabála Érenn; named Failinis in Oidheadh Chloinne Tuireann.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Lebor Gabála Érenn abad ke-12 tanpa nama; dinamai Failinis dalam Oidheadh Chloinne Tuireann.
claims.quote: The puppy is referred to as the "whelp of the royal smith of Ioruath" but otherwise unnamed in the 12th century Lebor Gabála Érenn ("Book of Invasions") version of the story

claims.statement: In the Fenian cycle Failinis (Fer Mac) belongs to three strangers from Iruaith; the Fíanna, Fionn mac Cumhaill; Ireland.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Siklus Fenian (Fenian cycle), Failinis (Fer Mac) milik tiga orang asing dari Iruaith; Fíanna, Fionn mac Cumhaill; Irlandia (Ireland).
claims.quote: Later on, Lugh's Failinis (var. Fer Mac) belonged to a foreign threesome from Iruaith that came to Ireland, and encountered by the Fíanna led by Fionn mac Cumhaill in the Fenian cycle.

claims.statement: Invincible, caught every wild beast, turned water into wine.
claims.statement_id: Tak terkalahkan, menangkap setiap binatang buas, mengubah air menjadi anggur.
claims.quote: The hound was invincible in battle, caught every wild beast it encountered, and could magically change any running water it bathed in into wine.

claims.statement: Eugene O'Curry: a transposition of Inis Fáil, an old name for Ireland.
claims.statement_id: Eugene O'Curry: pembalikan Inis Fáil, nama kuno Irlandia (Ireland).
claims.quote: Eugene O'Curry hypothesized the name Failinis to be a transposition of "Inis Fáil (Island of Fail)", an ancient name for Ireland

claims.statement: In the ballad: huge by day, a ball of fire by night.
claims.statement_id: Dalam balada: besar di siang hari, bola api di malam hari.
claims.quote: The hound of ballad was huge by day (able to "overcome fifty men"), but was a "thunderbolt, ball of fire" (Old Irish: caer thened ) by night.

claims.statement: ja article: water touching its fur becomes wine, or it spews liquor from its mouth.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ja: air yang menyentuh bulunya menjadi anggur, atau memuntahkan minuman keras.
claims.quote: とくに、その毛皮に触れる水をワインと化す（あるいは酒類を口から吐き出す）能力があるといわれる。

claims.statement: A fetch, a supernatural double of a living person; omen of death.
claims.statement_id: Fetch, kembaran gaib orang hidup; pertanda kematian.
claims.quote: A fetch is a supernatural double or an apparition of a living person. The sighting of a fetch is regarded as an inevitable omen, usually for impending death to oneself, or a loved one.

claims.statement: John and Michael Banim: appearing in the morning means long life.
claims.statement_id: John dan Michael Banim: muncul pagi hari pertanda umur panjang.
claims.quote: A sighting of a fetch is generally taken as a message of soon death, though John and Michael Banim report that if the double appears in the morning rather than the evening, it is instead a sign of a long life in store.

claims.statement: Like the Germanic doppelgänger and British wraith; Francis Grose, Northern England, Provincial Glossary 1787.
claims.statement_id: Mirip doppelgänger Jermanik (Germanic) dan wraith Inggris (British); Francis Grose, Inggris Utara (Northern England), Provincial Glossary 1787.
claims.quote: As such, it is similar to the Germanic doppelgänger and to some conceptions of the British wraith. Francis Grose associated the term with Northern England in his 1787 Provincial Glossary.

claims.statement: Fetch-life, a soul-fetching psychopomp, in Richard Stanyhurst's 1583 Aeneid translation.
claims.statement_id: Fetch-life, psikopompos penjemput jiwa, dalam terjemahan Aeneid oleh Richard Stanyhurst (1583).
claims.quote: the compound "fetch-life", evidently referring to a psychopomp who "fetches" the souls of the dying, is attested in Richard Stanyhurst's 1583 translation of the Aeneid

claims.statement: The fetch in early 19th-century Irish literature: The Fetches, Tales by the O'Hara Family (1825).
claims.statement_id: Fetch dalam sastra Irlandia (Irish) awal abad ke-19: The Fetches, Tales by the O'Hara Family (1825).
claims.quote: "The fetch superstition" is the topic of John and Michael Banim's Gothic story "The Fetches" from their 1825 work Tales by the O'Hara Family

claims.statement: es article: a supernatural double of a living person in Irish folklore.
claims.statement_id: Artikel es: kembaran gaib orang hidup dalam folklor Irlandia (irlandés).
claims.quote: Un fetch es un doble sobrenatural, aparición o fantasma de una persona viva en el folklore irlandés.

claims.statement: Táin Bó Cúailnge: Medb, queen of Connacht, seizes the bull Donn Cúailnge (Donn Cuailnge) from Cooley, Ulster; Ailill mac Máta.
claims.statement_id: Táin Bó Cúailnge: Medb, ratu Connacht, merampas banteng Donn Cúailnge (Donn Cuailnge) dari Cooley, Ulster; Ailill mac Máta.
claims.quote: The longest and most important story of the cycle is the Táin Bó Cúailnge or "Cattle Raid of Cooley", in which Medb raises an enormous army to invade the Cooley peninsula and steal the Ulaid's prize bull, Donn Cúailnge

claims.statement: In Irish mythology, Finnbhennach (Findbennach), bull of Ailill (Ailill mac Mágach), king of Connacht; means white-horned (Gwyn-gorniog); with Donn Cuailnge in the Táin Bó Cuailnge.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Irlandia (Irish, Iwerddon), Finnbhennach (Findbennach), banteng milik Ailill (Ailill mac Mágach), raja Connacht; berarti bertanduk putih (Gwyn-gorniog); bersama Donn Cuailnge dalam Táin Bó Cuailnge.
claims.quote: Ym mytholeg Iwerddon, tarw arbennig sy'n perthyn i Ailill mac Mágach, brenin Connacht, yw Finnbhennach (mae'r amrywiadau ar sillafiad yr enw yn cynnwys Findbennach). Ystyr ei enw yw "Gwyn-gorniog".

claims.statement: Birth in De chophur in da muccida: two swineherds of the fairy kings of Connacht and Munster.
claims.statement_id: Kelahiran dalam De chophur in da muccida: dua penggembala babi raja peri Connacht dan Munster.
claims.quote: Ceir hanes geni Finnbhennach yn y chwedl De chophur in da muccida, hanes dau feichiad (bugail moch) brenhinoedd Tylwyth Teg taleithiau Connacht a Munster.

claims.statement: Once Medb's, moved to Ailill's herd; killed by Donn Cuailnge in Connacht.
claims.statement_id: Dulu milik Medb, pindah ke kawanan Ailill; dibunuh Donn Cuailnge di Connacht.
claims.quote: Ar un adeg roedd y tarw yn perthyn i Medb, ond gan ei fod yn anfodlon cael gwraig yn berchennog arno, crwydrodd i ffwrdd ac ymuno â buches Ailill.

claims.statement: ga article: Fionnbheannach (Finnbennach), bull of king Ailill of Connacht; Rucht, swineherd of Ochall Ochne.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ga: Fionnbheannach (Finnbennach), banteng milik raja Ailill dari Connacht; Rucht, penggembala babi Ochall Ochne.
claims.quote: Sa Rúraíocht i Miotaseolaíocht na nGael, tarbh ghraíre olltorthúil ab ea Fionnbheannach (Sean-Ghaeilge Finnbennach)  le rí Ailill na gConnacht.

claims.statement: The two bulls fought; Fionnbheannach was killed, Donn Cuailnge mortally wounded.
claims.statement_id: Kedua banteng bertarung; Fionnbheannach terbunuh, Donn Cuailnge terluka parah.
claims.quote: Throid an dá tharbh; maraíodh Fionnbheannach agus fuair Donn Cuailnge goin a bháis.

claims.statement: Ghillie Dhu (Gille Dubh), a solitary male fairy of Scottish folklore, dark-haired, clothed in leaves and moss, origin of the ghillie suit; late 18th century; birch wood in the north-west Highlands; guards the forest, kind to children.
claims.statement_id: Ghillie Dhu (Gille Dubh), peri lelaki penyendiri folklor Skotlandia (Scottish, Scotland), rambut gelap, berpakaian daun dan lumut, asal nama ghillie suit; akhir abad ke-18; hutan birch Dataran Tinggi (Highlands) barat laut; menjaga hutan, baik kepada anak.
claims.quote: is a solitary male fairy described in Scottish folklore. He was said to be dark-haired, and clothed in leaves and moss, from which the ghillie suit got its name. He appears primarily in accounts from the late 18th century, living in a birch wood in the north-west Highlands of Scotland.

claims.statement: Ghillie, English equivalent of Scottish Gaelic gille (lad); dubh means dark.
claims.statement_id: Ghillie padanan Inggris (English) untuk kata Gaelik Skotlandia (Scottish Gaelic) gille (pemuda); dubh berarti gelap.
claims.quote: Ghillie is an English equivalent of the Scottish Gaelic word gille . English lexicographer Edward Dwelly lists gille as a "lad", "youth", or "boy"; with dubh meaning "dark" or "dark-haired".

claims.statement: Birch woods near Loch an Draing, Gairloch; Katharine Briggs: gentle mountain spirit, timid, wild, small.
claims.statement_id: Hutan birch dekat Loch an Draing, Gairloch; Katharine Briggs: roh gunung lembut, pemalu, liar, kecil.
claims.quote: He was said to live in the birch woods near Loch an Draing, in the north-west Highland area of Gairloch.

claims.statement: Jessie Macrae got lost; the Ghillie Dhu comforted her and led her home.
claims.statement_id: Jessie Macrae tersesat; Ghillie Dhu menghibur dan mengantarnya pulang.
claims.quote: The best known account of the Ghillie Dhu involves a girl named Jessie Macrae, who lived near the woods. She wandered into the woods and became lost as the sun went down.

claims.statement: Sir Hector Mackenzie of Gairloch and five Mackenzie dignitaries failed to catch him; per Patricia Monaghan never seen again.
claims.statement_id: Sir Hector Mackenzie dari (of) Gairloch dan lima bangsawan Mackenzie gagal memburunya; menurut Patricia Monaghan tak pernah terlihat lagi.
claims.quote: At some point, landowner Sir Hector Mackenzie of Gairloch invited a group of five Mackenzie dignitaries to hunt and capture the Ghillie Dhu, which he believed posed a threat.

claims.statement: eu article: the name ghillie suit (ghillie jantzia) is tied to this figure.
claims.statement_id: Artikel eu: nama ghillie suit (ghillie jantzia) terkait tokoh ini.
claims.quote: Hainbat hizkuntzatan "ghillie jantzia" izendapena pertsonaje honen izenarekin lotuta omen dago.

claims.statement: Gigelorum (Giol-Daoram), an insect of Scottish folklore, smallest creature, lives in a mite's ear.
claims.statement_id: Gigelorum (Giol-Daoram), serangga folklor Skotlandia (Scottish), makhluk terkecil, hidup di telinga tungau.
claims.quote: Gigelorum (or Giol-Daoram) is an insect of Scottish folklore. It was believed to be the smallest creature. No description or information is available about it except that it inhabits the ear of a mite.

claims.statement: Possibly based on the tiniest visible insect, the giolcam-daobhram.
claims.statement_id: Mungkin berdasar serangga terkecil yang terlihat, giolcam-daobhram.
claims.quote: Speculation exists that it may be based upon the tiniest insect that can be discerned by people possessing excellent eyesight, the giolcam-daobhram

claims.statement: Ronald Black, a one-time Celtic studies lecturer, suggests the creature may have been dreamt up by John Gregorson Campbell, folklorist and minister on Tiree, since Black found no authoritative source for it.
claims.statement_id: Ronald Black, mantan dosen studi Celtic, menduga makhluk ini mungkin khayalan folklorais sekaligus pendeta Tiree John Gregorson Campbell, karena ia tidak menemukan sumber yang berwibawa untuknya.
claims.quote: Ronald Black, a one time Celtic studies lecturer, author and journalist, suggests that the creature could be a figment of the imagination of folklorist and Tiree minister John Gregorson Campbell as he could trace no authoritative sources for it

claims.statement: it article: a tiny insect, the smallest animal, its habitat mites' ears.
claims.statement_id: Artikel it: serangga mungil, hewan terkecil, habitat di telinga tungau.
claims.quote: Si tratta di un insetto minuscolo, ritenuto essere il più piccolo animale esistente. Le sue caratteristiche sono ignote, eccezion fatta per il suo habitat, le orecchie degli acari.

claims.statement: it article: Ronald Black suggests an invention of John Gregorson Campbell.
claims.statement_id: Artikel it: Ronald Black menduga rekaan John Gregorson Campbell.
claims.quote: Ronald Black, docente occasionale di studi celtici, autore e giornalista, suggerisce come la creatura potrebbe essere un parto della mente del folclorista e ministro di Tiree John Gregorson Campbell

claims.statement: Per Campbell, the Giolcam-daoram, or Gigelorum, is the smallest of all animals; it makes its nest in the mite's ear and that is all that is known about it.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Campbell, Giolcam-daoram atau Gigelorum adalah yang terkecil dari semua hewan; ia bersarang di telinga tungau dan hanya itu yang diketahui tentangnya.
claims.quote: The Giolcam-daoram, or Gigelorum, is the smallest of all animals. It makes its nest in the mite's ear and that is all that is known about it.

claims.statement: Per the English Wikipedia article, the giolcam-daobhram is described as "an animalcule, the smallest supposable living thing".
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Wikipedia bahasa Inggris, giolcam-daobhram digambarkan sebagai "an animalcule, the smallest supposable living thing" (hewan mikro, makhluk hidup terkecil yang dapat dibayangkan).
claims.quote: the giolcam-daobhram, which is described as "an animalcule, the smallest supposable living thing".

claims.statement: Glas Gaibhnenn (Glas Ghaibhleann, Glas Gaivlen), in Irish folklore, is a prized fabulous cow of bounty that yields profuse quantities of milk; it is owned variously by a smith who may be named Gaivnin or by the hero Cian mac Cáinte, equivalent to Cian father of Lugh.
claims.statement_id: Glas Gaibhnenn (Glas Ghaibhleann, Glas Gaivlen), dalam cerita rakyat Irlandia, adalah sapi ajaib yang sangat berharga dan melimpah, menghasilkan susu dalam jumlah besar; pemiliknya berbeda-beda, yaitu pandai besi yang mungkin bernama Gaivnin atau pahlawan Cian mac Cáinte, yang setara dengan Cian ayah Lugh.
claims.quote: in Irish folklore, is a prized fabulous cow of bounty (fertility) that yields profuse quantities of milk. The cow is owned variously by a smith who may be named Gaivnin (hence reinforcing the notion that the cow's name is eponymous after him) or by the hero Cian mac Cáinte

claims.statement: The cow is stolen (or craftily regained) by Balar or Balor; the hero, to fulfil the quest to recover the cow, is transported by a banshee to a tower where Balor's daughter is sequestered, to produce a child destined to kill Balor.
claims.statement_id: Sapi itu dicuri (atau diperoleh kembali dengan akal) oleh Balar atau Balor; sang pahlawan, demi menunaikan misi mengambil kembali sapi, dibawa oleh banshee ke menara tempat putri Balor dikurung untuk melahirkan anak yang ditakdirkan membunuh Balor.
claims.quote: The cow is stolen (or craftily regained) by Balar or Balor the strong-smiter. The hero, in order to fulfill the quest to recover the cow, is transported by a banshee to a tower where Balor's daughter is sequestered, to produce a child destined to kill Balor.

claims.statement: Irish Wikipedia article: Patricia Monaghan wrote that Glas Ghaibhleann is a goddess often associated with rivers.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Wikipedia bahasa Irlandia: Patricia Monaghan menulis bahwa Glas Ghaibhleann adalah dewi yang sering dikaitkan dengan sungai.
claims.quote: Scríobh Patricia Monaghan gur bhandia í Glas Ghaibhleann ceangailte go minic le haibhneacha.

claims.statement: The full name means "Grey (cow) of the Smith" according to Larminie, and "Goibniu's Grey or Brindled (Cow)" according to Rhys.
claims.statement_id: Nama lengkapnya berarti "Sapi Kelabu milik Pandai Besi" menurut Larminie, dan "Sapi Kelabu atau Belang milik Goibniu" menurut Rhys.
claims.quote: Whereas the full name means "Grey (cow) of the Smith" according to Larminie, and "Goibniu's Grey or Brindled (Cow)" according to Rhys.

claims.statement: In one tradition, Lon the smith was for many years nourished by the cow Glas Gaibhneach, which he stole from Spain; the cow was pastured on the mountain of Sliabh-na-Glaise near the forge because no other place in Ireland was fertile enough.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu tradisi, Lon sang pandai besi bertahun-tahun hidup dari sapi Glas Gaibhneach yang ia curi dari Spanyol; sapi itu digembalakan di gunung Sliabh-na-Glaise dekat tempa karena tidak ada tempat lain di Irlandia yang cukup subur.
claims.quote: Lon the smith who took up residence here ... He was for many years nourished by the cow Glas Gaibhneach which he stole from Spain, and the cow was pastured on the mountain of Sliabh-na-Glaise, not far from the forge, for no other place in Ireland was fertile enough.

claims.statement: It was said this cow would fill any vessel with her milk at one milking; when two women wagered and a sieve was produced, her milk caused seven overflooding streams to pour forth.
claims.statement_id: Dikatakan sapi itu dengan susunya memenuhi bejana apa pun dalam satu kali perah; ketika dua perempuan bertaruh dan sebuah saringan diajukan, susunya menyebabkan tujuh aliran meluap.
claims.quote: This cow would fill with her milk any vessel,.. at one milking ... when a sieve was produced, the cow's milk caused seven overflooding streams to pour forth.

claims.statement: It was said the cow's hoofs were reversed, and the backward tracks always fooled the would-be cattle thieves in pursuit.
claims.statement_id: Dikatakan kuku sapi itu terbalik, sehingga jejak yang mengarah ke belakang selalu mengelabui para calon pencuri ternak yang mengejarnya.
claims.quote: Also it was said "the hoofs of this cow were reversed", and the backward tracks always fooled the potential cattle-thieves in pursuit.

claims.statement: In Lady Gregory's version, Cian had a wonderful cow, the Glas Gaibhnenn, whose milk never failed; everyone who heard of her coveted her and many had tried to steal her, so she had to be watched night and day.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Lady Gregory, Cian punya sapi ajaib, Glas Gaibhnenn, yang susunya tak pernah habis; semua yang mendengarnya mengingininya dan banyak yang mencoba mencurinya, sehingga ia harus dijaga siang dan malam.
claims.quote: Now Cian had a wonderful cow, the Glas Gaibhnenn, and her milk never failed. And every one that heard of her coveted her, and many had tried to steal her away, so that she had to be watched night and day.

claims.statement: In Lady Gregory's version, Balor had long set his mind on the Glas Gaibhnenn but had never been able to get near her; when he saw Samthainn holding the cow he put on the appearance of a little boy with red hair.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Lady Gregory, Balor lama mengincar Glas Gaibhnenn tetapi tak pernah bisa mendekatinya; ketika melihat Samthainn memegang sapi itu, ia menyamar menjadi anak lelaki kecil berambut merah.
claims.quote: Now Balor had set his mind for a long time on the Glas Gaibhnenn, but he had never been able to get near her up to this time. And he was watching not far off, and when he saw Samthainn holding the cow, he put on the appearance of a little boy, having red hair

claims.statement: In Lady Gregory's version, as soon as Balor got the halter in his hand he dragged the Glas to the strand and across the sea to his own island.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Lady Gregory, begitu Balor memegang tali kekang, ia membawa Glas itu ke pantai dan menyeberangi laut ke pulaunya sendiri.
claims.quote: no sooner did Balor get the halter in his hand than he set out, dragging the Glas along with him, to the strand, and across the sea to his own island.

claims.statement: In Lady Gregory's version, a Druid told Cian that so long as Balor lived the cow would never be brought back, for no one would go within reach of his Evil Eye.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Lady Gregory, seorang Druid memberi tahu Cian bahwa selama Balor hidup sapi itu tak akan bisa dibawa kembali, karena tak seorang pun berani mendekati jangkauan Mata Jahatnya.
claims.quote: When Cian saw his brother coming in he rushed out, and there he saw Balor and the Glas out in the sea. ... it is what the Druid told him, that so long as Balor lived, the cow would never be brought back, for no one would go within reach of his Evil Eye.

claims.statement: Gwyllgi (gwyllt wild / gwyll twilight + ci dog), mythical dog of Wales, phantom mastiff or black wolf, blazing red eyes.
claims.statement_id: Gwyllgi (gwyllt liar / gwyll senja + ci anjing), anjing mitos Wales, hantu mastiff atau serigala hitam, mata merah menyala.
claims.quote: compound noun of either gwyllt "wild" or gwyll "twilight" + ci "dog") is a mythical dog from Wales that appears as a frightful apparition of a mastiff or black wolf with baleful breath and blazing red eyes.

claims.statement: Welsh incarnation of the black dog of English folklore.
claims.statement_id: Perwujudan Welsh anjing hitam folklor Inggris (English).
claims.quote: It is the Welsh incarnation of the black dog figure of English folklore.

claims.statement: Also called Cwn Annwfn, Cwn Annwn (dogs of the otherworld), Cwn Cyrff (corpse dog).
claims.statement_id: Disebut Cwn Annwfn, Cwn Annwn (anjing dunia lain), Cwn Cyrff (anjing mayat).
claims.quote: The Gwyllgi are also called Cwn Annwfn or Cwn Annwn (meaning "dogs of the otherworld") and Cwn Cyrff ("corpse dog").

claims.statement: Sightings in north-east Wales: Nant y Garth near Llandegla, Denbighshire; Marchwiel, Wrexham.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan di Wales timur laut: Nant y Garth dekat Llandegla, Denbighshire; Marchwiel, Wrexham.
claims.quote: Specifically, the Nant y Garth pass located near Llandegla in Denbighshire. It has even been spotted as far away as Marchwiel in Wrexham

claims.statement: it article: The Dog of Darkness, The Black Hound of Destiny; appears on lonely roads at night.
claims.statement_id: Artikel it: The Dog of Darkness, The Black Hound of Destiny; muncul di jalan sepi malam hari.
claims.quote: Viene spesso chiamato "The Dog of Darkness"(il cane dell'oscurità) o "The Black Hound of Destiny"(il mastino nero del destino), i ritrovi prediletti per le apparizioni sono strade solitarie durante la notte.

claims.statement: Blood of the Earth by Faith Hunter.
claims.statement_id: Blood of the Earth karya Faith Hunter.
claims.quote: In Blood of the Earth, by Faith Hunter, many members of the local cult-like church have been turned into gwyllgi and capture the main character, Nell.

claims.statement: Houles fairies (Gwenn fadoù), Channel coast from Cancale to Tréveneuc, Upper Brittany, the Channel Islands, Cotentin; coastal caves called houles; immortal, powerful, salt-sensitive; Breton.
claims.statement_id: Peri houle (Gwenn fadoù), pesisir Selat Inggris (Channel) dari Cancale ke Tréveneuc, Haute-Bretagne (Upper Brittany), Kepulauan Channel (Channel Islands), Cotentin; gua pantai houle; abadi, kuat, peka garam; Breton.
claims.quote: are fairies specific to the Channel coast, stretching from Cancale to Tréveneuc in Upper Brittany, to the Channel Islands, and known from a few fragments of stories in the Cotentin region. They live in coastal caves and caverns known as houles. Reputed to be magnificent, immortal and very powerful, they are sensitive to salt.

claims.statement: Benevolent, communal, launder, bake bread, tend flocks, served by warrior goblins called Fions.
claims.statement_id: Baik hati, hidup berkelompok, mencuci, memanggang roti, menggembala, dilayani goblin prajurit Fions.
claims.quote: Rather benevolent, the swell fairies described in local stories live in communities, do their own laundry, bake their own bread or tend their own flocks, marry male fairies and are served by warrior goblins called Fions.

claims.statement: Help humans with food and enchanted objects; angry when disrespected.
claims.statement_id: Membantu manusia dengan makanan dan benda ajaib; marah bila tak dihormati.
claims.quote: They come to the aid of humans in many ways, providing food and enchanted objects, but get angry if anyone disrespects them or acquires the power to see their disguises without their consent.

claims.statement: Paul Sébillot, French and Gallo, some fifty tales; semi-divinities worshipped by the Upper Bretons.
claims.statement_id: Paul Sébillot, bahasa Prancis (French) dan Gallo, sekitar lima puluh kisah; setengah dewa dipuja orang Haute-Bretagne (Upper Bretons).
claims.quote: Paul Sébillot's collections, in French and Gallo, have yielded some fifty tales and fragments of legends evoking these creatures. The houles fairies, considered "semi-divinities", were probably worshipped locally by the Upper Bretons.

claims.statement: Belief waned in the 19th century due to Christianity and teachers.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan merosot pada abad ke-19 karena Kristen (Christianity) dan guru.
claims.quote: Belief in them waned considerably in the 19th century, under the religious influence of Christianity and teachers.

claims.statement: de article: Grottenfeen (fées des houles), Breton folklore, Cancale to Tréveneuc, Haute-Bretagne, Guernsey; France.
claims.statement_id: Artikel de: Grottenfeen (fées des houles), folklor Breton, Cancale hingga Tréveneuc, Haute-Bretagne, Guernsey; Prancis.
claims.quote: Grottenfeen (französisch fées des houles, englisch houles fairies) sind mythische Wesen aus der bretonischen Folklore, die entlang der Kanalküste, von Cancale bis Tréveneuc in der Haute-Bretagne sowie auf den Kanalinseln wie Guernsey, beheimatet sind.

claims.statement: Beautiful, powerful, nearly immortal, made mortal by contact with salt.
claims.statement_id: Indah, kuat, hampir abadi, menjadi fana karena kontak dengan garam.
claims.quote: Sie werden als schöne, mächtige und fast unsterbliche Wesen beschrieben, die jedoch durch den Kontakt mit Salz sterblich werden können.

claims.statement: Jimmy Squarefoot, a bipedal pig-headed creature of Manx folklore, Isle of Man.
claims.statement_id: Jimmy Squarefoot, makhluk berkaki dua berkepala babi folklor Manx, Pulau Man (Isle of Man).
claims.quote: In Manx folklore, Jimmy Squarefoot is a legendary bipedal pig-headed creature living on the Isle of Man.

claims.statement: He is thought to have once been ridden by an unnamed Foawr, a type of stone-throwing giant living on Cronk yn Irree Lhaa who may have been the husband of the Caillagh ny Groamagh.
claims.statement_id: Konon pernah ditunggangi seorang Foawr (jenis raksasa pelempar batu) tanpa nama yang tinggal di Cronk yn Irree Lhaa dan mungkin suami Caillagh ny Groamagh.
claims.quote: He is thought to have once been ridden by an unnamed Foawr, a type of stone-throwing giant, living on Cronk yn Irree Lhaa who may have been the husband of the Caillagh ny Groamagh.

claims.statement: Said to live in the hills of Arbory and Malew, mainly near the bridge over the Grenaby river; said to have a cave near South Barrule through which he takes humans to the underworld.
claims.statement_id: Dikatakan tinggal di perbukitan Arbory dan Malew, terutama dekat jembatan di atas sungai Grenaby; ia disebut punya gua di dekat South Barrule dan membawa manusia melewatinya ke dunia bawah.
claims.quote: Jimmy Squarefoot is said to live in the hills of Arbory and Malew, mainly near the bridge over the Grenaby river. He is said to have a cave near South Barrule, and takes humans through it to the underworld.

claims.statement: May also be linked with the story of a buggane in Rushen that could transform between a man and a black pig; the name "Jimmy Squarefoot" was also used by sailors for the devil in the late 1800s and early 1900s.
claims.statement_id: Mungkin terkait dengan kisah buggane di Rushen yang bisa berganti wujud antara manusia dan babi hitam; nama "Jimmy Squarefoot" juga dipakai pelaut untuk menyebut iblis pada akhir 1800-an dan awal 1900-an.
claims.quote: Jimmy Squarefoot may also be linked with the story of a buggane in Rushen which was able to transform between a man and a black pig. The name "Jimmy Squarefoot" was also used by sailors to refer to the devil during the late 1800s and early 1900s.

claims.statement: His large feet, wrapped in calico bands, look square, hence the name "Squarefoot" (per the German Wikipedia article).
claims.statement_id: Kakinya yang besar dibalut pita kaliko dan tampak persegi, sehingga bernama "Squarefoot" (menurut artikel Wikipedia bahasa Jerman).
claims.quote: Seine großen Füße sind mit Kaliko-Bändern umwickelt und wirken quadratisch, daher der Name „Squarefoot“.

claims.statement: Per Gill, Jimmy Squarefoot was broadly a man with a pig's head and face and two great tusks like a boar, and he haunted all round the Grenaby district.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Gill, Jimmy Squarefoot pada dasarnya adalah manusia berkepala dan berwajah babi dengan dua taring besar seperti babi hutan, dan ia menghantui seluruh daerah Grenaby.
claims.quote: Broadly speaking, Jimmy Squarefoot was a man with a pig's head and face, "and he had two great tusks like a boar." He haunted all round the Grenaby district. ... (source: A Manx Scrapbook by W Walter Gill (1929)

claims.statement: Per Gill, the giant, whose name is forgotten, rode Jimmy in his pig-form about the country and over the sea.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Gill, si raksasa (yang namanya terlupakan) menunggangi Jimmy dalam wujud babinya keliling negeri dan menyeberangi laut.
claims.quote: This giant, whose name is regrettably forgotten, rode Jimmy in his pig-form about the country and over the sea ... (source: A Manx Scrapbook by W Walter Gill (1929)

claims.statement: Per Gill, there is something engaging about Jimmy when he used to charge out at wayfarers with gleaming tusks and gnashing fangs; he seems to have an affinity with water.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Gill, ada sesuatu yang menarik pada Jimmy ketika dulu ia menyerbu para pejalan kaki dengan taring berkilau dan gigi bergemeletuk; ia tampaknya punya kedekatan dengan air.
claims.quote: there is something engaging about Jimmy when he used to charge out at wayfarers with gleaming tusks and gnashing fangs. ... For he seems to have an affinity with water ... (source: A Manx Scrapbook by W Walter Gill (1929)

claims.statement: Gill writes that he has never been able to learn how Jimmy got the sobriquet "Squarefoot".
claims.statement_id: Gill menulis bahwa ia tidak pernah berhasil mengetahui bagaimana Jimmy mendapat julukan "Squarefoot".
claims.quote: How he got the sobriquet of "Squarefoot" I have never been able to learn. ... (source: A Manx Scrapbook by W Walter Gill (1929)

claims.statement: Per the German Wikipedia article, Jimmy Squarefoot is usually a peaceful wanderer.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Wikipedia bahasa Jerman, Jimmy Squarefoot biasanya adalah pengembara yang damai.
claims.quote: Laut der Folklore der Manx lebt Jimmy Squarefoot, eine legendäre zweibeinige schweineköpfige Kreatur, auf der Isle of Man in der Irischen See. Es ist für gewöhnlich ein friedlicher Wanderer.

claims.statement: The German Wikipedia article says that elsewhere Jimmy Squarefoot was at first himself depicted as a stone-throwing giant who rode a pig.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Wikipedia bahasa Jerman menyebut bahwa di tempat lain Jimmy Squarefoot pada mulanya digambarkan sendiri sebagai raksasa pelempar batu yang menunggang babi.
claims.quote: An anderer Stelle wird geschildert, dass Jimmy Squarefoot anfangs selber als steinewerfender Riese dargestellt wurde, der auf einem Schwein ritt.

claims.statement: Jimmy Squarefoot is also the name of Monster in My Pocket #80 and of a character in the 2007 PlayStation 3 video game Folklore.
claims.statement_id: Jimmy Squarefoot juga nama Monster in My Pocket #80 dan tokoh dalam gim video PlayStation 3 Folklore tahun 2007.
claims.quote: Jimmy Squarefoot is also the name of Monster in My Pocket #80 as well as a character in the 2007 PlayStation 3 video game Folklore.

claims.statement: Kilmoulis, Anglo-Scottish border folklore, ugly brownie of mills; huge nose, no mouth.
claims.statement_id: Kilmoulis, folklor perbatasan Inggris-Skotlandia (Anglo-Scottish), brownie buruk rupa di penggilingan; hidung besar, tanpa mulut.
claims.quote: A kilmoulis is, in the folklore of the Anglo-Scottish border, an ugly version of the brownie who is said to haunt mills. He has an enormous nose and no mouth. This lack of an orifice forces him to inhale his food through his nose.

claims.statement: Works hard for the miller, loves pranks.
claims.statement_id: Bekerja keras untuk tukang giling, gemar iseng.
claims.quote: The Kilmoulis works hard for the miller, but also delights in tricks and pranks. While his pranks may be a hindrance, he is generally enough help to offset the food he eats and the disturbances he causes.

claims.statement: Dungeons & Dragons; video game Folklore; Andrzej Sapkowski's Witcher books.
claims.statement_id: Dungeons & Dragons; permainan video Folklore; buku Witcher karya Andrzej Sapkowski.
claims.quote: In popular culture, it was used in the Dungeons & Dragons game as a fey creature. A version of the kilmoulis appears in the video game Folklore. Kilmoulis also appears as a sentient monster in Andrzej Sapkowski's Witcher books.

claims.statement: es article: a grotesque brownie of Anglo-Scottish folklore, haunting mills.
claims.statement_id: Artikel es: versi grotesk brownie dalam folklor Inggris-Skotlandia, di penggilingan.
claims.quote: Un Kilmoulis es una criatura mítica perteneciente al folclore anglo-escocés, considerado como una versión grotesca de los brownie (espíritus familiares) que se dice rondan en los molinos.

claims.statement: Per Henderson, Killmoulis is a peculiar species of Brownie who haunts the mill and resides in the killogee, the space before the fireplace in the kiln.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Henderson, Killmoulis adalah jenis Brownie yang istimewa, yang menghantui penggilingan dan tinggal di killogee, yaitu ruang di depan perapian di tungku pengering (kiln).
claims.quote: Killmoulis is a peculiar species of Brownie, who haunts the mill, and resides in the killogee, or space before the fireplace in the kiln.

claims.statement: Per Henderson, this sprite appears to have no mouth, yet the rhymes he quotes testify to his taste for swine's-flesh.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Henderson, makhluk ini tampaknya tidak punya mulut, namun sajak-sajak yang ia kutip menunjukkan kesukaannya pada daging babi.
claims.quote: he appears to have no mouth ... yet the following rhymes testify to his taste for swine's-flesh

claims.statement: Per Henderson, Killmoulis takes the liveliest interest in the miller and his mill and wails piteously should misfortune threaten them, yet often torments the goodman by throwing ashes out when shelled oats (sheelin) are spread out to dry.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Henderson, Killmoulis sangat peduli pada pemilik penggilingan dan penggilingannya, meratap pilu bila bahaya mengancam, tetapi sering menyiksa sang tuan rumah dengan melempar abu keluar ketika gandum kupas (sheelin) dijemur.
claims.quote: Killmoulis takes the liveliest interest in the miller and his mill. Should any misfortune threaten them he will wail piteously. At the same time he often torments the goodman sorely by throwing ... or ashes out when sheelin or shelled oats are spread out to dry

claims.statement: Per Henderson, he will not leave off his mischievous tricks till the miller calls out to him, whereupon he appears, puffing and blowing, in the shape of an old man with no mouth but an enormous nose.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Henderson, ia tidak berhenti berbuat jahil sampai sang pemilik penggilingan memanggilnya, lalu ia muncul terengah-engah berwujud lelaki tua tanpa mulut tetapi berhidung sangat besar.
claims.quote: nor will he leave off his mischievous tricks till the miller calls out, ... on which he appears, puffing and blowing, in the shape of an old man, the mouth wanting, but with an enormous nose.

claims.statement: Per Henderson, Killmoulis will never quit his favourite corner except to thrash the corn in great emergency or to ride for the howdie (midwife) when the miller's wife needs her services.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Henderson, Killmoulis tidak pernah meninggalkan sudut kesukaannya kecuali untuk mengirik gandum dalam keadaan darurat atau menunggang kuda memanggil bidan ketika istri pemilik penggilingan membutuhkannya.
claims.quote: Killmoulis will never quit the ... his favourite corner, except to thrash the corn in great emergency, or to ride for the howdie, when the miller's wife needs her services

claims.statement: Per Henderson, every mill was haunted by its own Killmoulis.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Henderson, setiap penggilingan dihantui Killmoulis-nya sendiri.
claims.quote: Every mill was haunted by its own Killmoulis

claims.statement: Per Henderson, in Roxburghshire Killmoulis is drawn into the "blue clue" divination: towards the end of the winding he holds the thread, and he will snort out the name of your future spouse.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Henderson, di Roxburghshire Killmoulis ikut terlibat dalam ramalan "blue clue" (gulungan benang biru): menjelang akhir penggulungan ia memegang benang, dan ia akan mendengus menyebut nama calon pasangan hidup.
claims.quote: In Roxburghshire Killmoulis is thus drawn into the spell of the ... Towards the end of the winding Killmoulis will hold the thread. You must ask ... and he will snort out the name of your future spouse.

claims.statement: Henderson writes that one would suppose he took his name from the kiln, but Mr. Wilkie considers it to mean the miller's servant.
claims.statement_id: Henderson menulis bahwa orang akan mengira namanya berasal dari kiln (tungku pengering), tetapi Mr. Wilkie menganggapnya berarti pelayan pemilik penggilingan.
claims.quote: One would suppose that he took his name from the kiln, but Mr. Wilkie considers ... to mean the miller's servant.

claims.statement: Krasnoludek (krasnal), Polish name for a mythical gnome or dwarf, pointy red hats.
claims.statement_id: Krasnoludek (krasnal), nama Polandia (Polish) untuk gnome atau kurcaci mitologis, topi merah runcing.
claims.quote: Krasnoludek or krasnal is the Polish name for a mythological type of gnome or dwarf, common in many Polish and translated folk tales. They resemble small humans and wear pointy red hats.

claims.statement: Germanic origin, in Polish folktales from the 16th or 17th century.
claims.statement_id: Asal Jermanik (Germanic), muncul dalam dongeng Polandia abad ke-16 atau ke-17.
claims.quote: The mythological dwarf is of Germanic origin and appeared in Polish folktales in the 16th or 17th century.

claims.statement: From Old Polish krasny (red, nice-looking) and ludek (small person).
claims.statement_id: Dari bahasa Polandia kuno (Old Polish) krasny (merah, elok) dan ludek (orang kecil).
claims.quote: The word krasnoludek comes from the old Polish krasny, kraśny ("red, colorful," "nice-looking," or "good") and Polish ludek (small person or human-like creature).

claims.statement: Wrocław: Orange Alternative statue, anti-communist movement; hundreds of dwarf statues.

claims.quote: In the city of Wrocław, a bronze statue honoring the Orange Alternative, an anti-communist social movement whose mascot is a krasnoludek dwarf, has inspired hundreds of other dwarf statues around the city

claims.statement: ru article: a dwarf folk of Polish and Belarusian mythology (Skrzaty), from belief in ancestors' souls; home guardians.

claims.statement_id: Dalam daftar bentuk dialek Polandia yang disusun Kregždys, krasnyludek/kraśnoludek diberi arti makhluk kecil berwujud manusia yang memakai topi merah runcing, tinggal di dalam tanah, lubang, dan reruntuhan, serta menolong manusia yang membutuhkan.
claims.quote: krasnyludek, kraśnoludek / kraśnyludek 'a small human-shaped being who wears pointy red hat, dwells in the earth, in pits, ruins and all kinds of holes; helpful to humans when they are in need'

claims.statement: In the same list, the dialect form krasnoludek/krusnalek is glossed as a dwarfish man of the size of a fly or a bee who lives in a mousehole.

claims.statement: The dialect form krosnalek is glossed as a dwarf of the size of an insect who lives in a mousehole and gets out to spree on the night of the full moon; harmless to humans, but in the moment of fright it becomes a giant.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk dialek krosnalek diberi arti kurcaci seukuran serangga yang tinggal di lubang tikus dan keluar berpesta pada malam bulan purnama; tidak berbahaya bagi manusia, tetapi menjadi raksasa saat ketakutan.
claims.quote: krosnalek, (pl.) krosnalki 'a dwarf of a size of an insect who lives in a mousehole and gets out from there to spree in the night of the full moon; harmless to humans, but in the moment of fright it becomes a giant'

claims.statement: Per the Wrocław tourism site, in Polish folk demonology it is difficult to find a single term for the dwarf figure; each region uses a different name and attributes different behaviour to it.

claims.quote: In Polish folk demonology it is difficult to find a homogeneous term for the dwarf figure. Actually, each region uses a different name and attributes different behavior to it.

claims.statement: Per the Wrocław tourism site, in the second half of 2020 there were about 360 dwarf figures in Wrocław.

claims.statement: Morvarc'h (sea horse, Breton), of Breton legend; Charles Guyot, Morvark, city of Ys, 1926; Malgven's, Queen of the North, given to King Gradlon. Two folktales reworked in the 19th and 20th centuries.
claims.statement_id: Morvarc'h (kuda laut, Breton), legenda Bretagne (Breton, Prancis); Charles Guyot, Morvark, kota Ys, 1926; milik Malgven, Ratu Utara (Queen of the North), untuk Raja (King) Gradlon. Dua dongeng digubah ulang abad ke-19 dan ke-20 (19th, 20th).
claims.quote: is the name of a fabulous horse of Breton legend found in two folktales reworked in the 19th and 20th centuries. Though its name appears in older sources, it was invented or reinterpreted by Charles Guyot, who named it Morvark in his version of the legend of the city of Ys in 1926. It belongs to the "Queen of the North" Malgven, who gives it to her husband King Gradlon.

claims.statement: Gallops on the waves, black coat, breathes flames.
claims.statement_id: Berlari di atas ombak, bulu hitam, menyemburkan api.
claims.quote: Endowed with the ability to gallop on the waves, Morvarc'h is described as having a black coat and as breathing flames through its nostrils.

claims.statement: Killed by an arrow turned by Dahud's spell, Malgven's daughter; its ears on King Marc'h of Cornouaille.
claims.statement_id: Tewas oleh panah yang dibelokkan sihir Dahud, putri Malgven; telinganya di kepala Raja (King) Marc'h dari Cornouaille.
claims.quote: In the course of a deer hunt it is killed by its own rider's arrow, which has been turned around by the spell of Dahud, the daughter of Malgven. She then puts the ears of the horse Morvarc'h on the head of King Marc'h, who seeks in vain to hide them.

claims.statement: Equestrian statues at Argol and Saint Corentin's Cathedral, Quimper.
claims.statement_id: Patung berkuda di Argol dan Katedral Saint-Corentin (Saint Corentin's Cathedral), Quimper.
claims.quote: it is the subject of equestrian statues in the town of Argol and in Saint Corentin's Cathedral in Quimper.

claims.statement: Morvarc'h means sea horse; Grégoire de Rostrenen's dictionary, 1732.
claims.statement_id: Morvarc'h berarti kuda laut; kamus Grégoire de Rostrenen, 1732.
claims.quote: The name Morvarc'h means "sea horse" or "marine horse" in Breton. It appears in Grégoire de Rostrenen's [fr] dictionary, published in 1732.

claims.statement: es article: gallops on the waves and breathes flames from its nostrils.

claims.statement_id: Nimerigar, orang kecil folklor Shoshone, Pegunungan Rocky (Rocky Mountains), Amerika Utara (North America); agresif, panah beracun.
claims.quote: The Nimerigar are a legendary race of little people found in the folklore of the Shoshone people of North America's Rocky Mountains. According to Shoshone tales, the Nimerigar were an aggressive people who would shoot poisoned arrows from tiny bows.

claims.statement: Means people eaters in Shoshone and Paiute; killed the sick with a blow to the head.
claims.statement_id: Berarti pemakan manusia dalam bahasa Shoshone dan Paiute; membunuh yang sakit dengan pukulan kepala.
claims.quote: Nimerigar roughly translated from Shoshone and Paiute languages means "people eaters". They were believed to kill their own people with a blow to the head if they became too ill to be a participating member of their society.

claims.statement: San Pedro Mountains mummy 1932, 14 in, cave 60 miles south of Casper, Wyoming.
claims.statement_id: Mumi San Pedro Mountains 1932, 14 inci, gua 60 mil selatan Casper, Wyoming.
claims.quote: the reality of Nimerigar tales was called into question in 1932 with the discovery of the San Pedro Mountains mummy, a 14 in (36 cm)-tall mummy (6.5 in (17 cm) seated) found in a cave 60 miles south of Casper, Wyoming.

claims.statement: University of Wyoming: an anencephalic infant; second mummy by George Gill in the 1990s; Native American DNA.

claims.quote: When examined by the University of Wyoming, the body was found to be that of a deceased anencephalic infant "whose cranial deformity gave it the appearance of a miniature adult."

claims.statement: de article: a race of small warlike people per Shoshone tales, formerly in Wyoming.

claims.quote: Als Nimerigar wird eine Rasse kleiner kriegerischer Menschen bezeichnet, die nach Erzählungen der Schoschonen früher das Gebiet von Wyoming besiedelt haben sollen.

claims.quote: is a mythical water horse of primarily Shetland folklore where it is also referred to as a shoepultie or shoopiltee on some parts of the islands. A nocturnal creature that is always of a male gender

claims.statement: Wheel-like tail; unlike the each-uisge or nuckelavee, gentle and prankish.
claims.statement_id: Ekor seperti roda; tak seperti each-uisge atau nuckelavee, wataknya lembut dan suka iseng.
claims.quote: He is easily recognised by his distinctive wheel-like tail and, unlike his evil counterparts the each-uisge or the nuckelavee, has a fairly gentle disposition being more prone to playing pranks and making mischief rather than having malicious intents.

claims.statement: Assumes many disguises, usually an attractive horse, never human; near watermills.
claims.statement_id: Menyamar dalam banyak wujud, biasanya kuda menarik, tak pernah manusia; dekat kincir air.
claims.quote: The entity was capable of assuming many disguises but generally favoured the form of an attractive horse; he never assumed a human form.

claims.statement: es article: mythical water horse of Shetland, nocturnal, always male.
claims.statement_id: Artikel es: kuda air mitos Shetland, nokturnal, selalu jantan.
claims.quote: El nuggle, njuggle o neugle es un caballo de agua mítico del folklore de las Islas Shetland, una criatura nocturna que siempre es macho.

claims.statement: Tricks a passer-by into mounting, then heads for deep water.
claims.statement_id: Memperdaya orang menungganginya lalu lari ke air terdalam.
claims.quote: If the nuggle had successfully tricked an unsuspecting passer-by into mounting him, usually by pretending to be tame and standing tranquilly at the side of a path, he would immediately make for the nearest deep water.

claims.statement: Jessie Saxby: fear of the nuggle kept children from deep water and watermills.
claims.statement_id: Jessie Saxby: ketakutan akan nuggle menjauhkan anak dari air dalam dan kincir air.
claims.quote: Jessie Saxby suggests fear of the nuggle prevented children venturing too close to deep water or watermills

claims.statement: Simonside Dwarfs, Brownmen, Bogles, Duergar; English folklore; Simonside Hills, Northumberland, northern England; leader Heslop.
claims.statement_id: Kurcaci Simonside (Simonside Dwarfs), Brownmen, Bogles, Duergar; folklor Inggris (English); Simonside Hills, Northumberland, Inggris utara; pemimpin Heslop.
claims.quote: The Simonside Dwarfs, also known as Brownmen, Bogles and Duergar, are in English folklore a race of dwarfs, particularly associated with the Simonside Hills of Northumberland, in northern England. Their leader was said to be known as Heslop.

claims.statement: Frederick Grice, The Duergar (1944): short, lambskin coat, moleskin trousers, moss hat with a feather.
claims.statement_id: Frederick Grice, The Duergar (1944): pendek, mantel kulit domba, celana kulit tikus mondok, topi lumut berbulu.
claims.quote: In Frederick Grice's telling of the traditional story The Duergar in Folk Tales of the North Country (1944), one of them is described as being short, wearing a lambskin coat, moleskin trousers and shoes, and a hat made of moss stuck with a feather.

claims.statement: Led travellers astray after dark with torches into bogs, like a Will-o'-the-wisp; vanished at dawn.
claims.statement_id: Menyesatkan pengembara setelah gelap dengan obor ke rawa, mirip Will-o'-the-wisp; lenyap saat fajar.
claims.quote: They delighted in leading travellers astray, especially after dark, often carrying lighted torches to lead them into bogs, rather like a Will-o'-the-wisp. The menacing creatures would often disappear at dawn.

claims.statement: Duergar from Anglo-Scottish Border dialect plus Norse -ar, or Old Norse dvergar.

claims.quote: In the 2004 film Van Helsing, the Duergi are the minions of Count Dracula.

claims.statement_id: Skuld (Sculd, Skulde, Skulda), putri legenda Skandinavia (Scandinavian), saudari tiri Raja Denmark (Danish, Denmark) Hrólfr Kraki, istri Hjörvarðr.
claims.quote: was a princess of Scandinavian legend, the sister or half-sister of the legendary Danish King Hrólfr Kraki and the wife of Hrólfr's killer, Hjörvarðr

claims.statement: The name Skuld, shared with the norn, from Old Norse skulla; Hrólfs saga kraka.

claims.quote: The name Skuld (which the princess shares with Skuld, one of the norns in Norse mythology) is derived from the Old Norse verb skulla, "need/ought to be/shall be"

claims.statement: A great sorceress using seiðr; an army of warriors, criminals, elves and norns.

claims.quote: She was a great sorceress and used seiðr (witchcraft) to hide the great muster from Hrólfr and his champions.

claims.statement: Hjörvarðr was also killed; Skuld became Queen of Denmark but ruled badly and briefly.
